member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiEvent.TryFromShared(OpenIGI.Game.Ai.HumanAiEvent@,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiEvent@)
member.summary: Another game's event in this game's terms (, numbered as ): the engine's events in the same order, Project I.G.I.'s AIEVENT_COMBAT (7) without a counterpart, so every later one a number lower here.
member.returns: Whether this game has the event.

remarks.para: The flags are the engine's own bits, which both games test alike; the human ones are answered by the event's source, whichever game's human it is (). A near miss is not taken: this game hears another's rounds through the level's bodies.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiEvent.FromShared(OpenIGI.Game.Ai.HumanAiEvent@)
member.summary: Another game's event as this game's own humans would raise it: a gunshot as this game's guns tell of one, a round striking the ground as its bullets do, and anything else as reads it.
member.returns: This game's events, in the order its own would be sent; none where it has no such event.

remarks.para: A gun here () raises a shot and a shot along its line at its own range, and, louder than , a loud shot first, seen far off by whoever has the gun in view: so another game's gunshot is those, at its own range and along its line of fire, with this game's flags.
A bullet striking here raises its strike (), pointing back up its flight; a ground impact with a flight is a round's, and is that. One without is a landing, and is read as it is.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiEvent.TryToShared(OpenIGI.Game.Ai.HumanAiEvent@)
member.summary: This event in the engine's shared terms (), for another game's humans: the inverse of , every event from AIEVENT_ALARMON on a number higher there.
member.param: Receives the event, this one whole as its context.
member.returns: Whether the other game has the event.
member.remarks: A near miss is not given: another game hears this one's rounds go by through the level's bodies, as this one hears theirs.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiGraph
member.summary: An AI graph's nodes and links as Graph_ParseGraphStream (igi2 0x59B4B0) reads them from a level's graphs/graph<id>.dat.

remarks.para: The file is the named stream I.G.I. 1 also writes (, each value a field hash, a type and the value), read by a callback per field into one staged node. I.G.I. 2 adds two node fields, nNodeOnTerrain and vNodeLightValue, has no route table (its soldiers search the graph), and keeps up to 2000 nodes where I.G.I. 1 kept 1000.

nNodeID clears the staged node (Graph_NodeIDCallback, 0x59AA20); nNodeCriteria makes it (Graph_NodeCriteriaCallback, 0x59AC50, into Graph_CreateNode, 0x59A040), its criteria evaluated as a one-line script. eLinkType makes a link from the last two ids read (Graph_CreateLink, 0x59A610).

member.content: The queries soldiers ask a graph as the level runs (aigraph.c, graph.c).

member.summary: A graph another game's level placed: the shared format's nodes where that game put them in the world, and its links.
member.param: The graph, read and placed by the game whose level it is.
What carries the graph, when the placing game left its nodes in the carrier's frame; the nodes then ride it, as a graph under one of the game's own movers does. for a graph placed in the world.
member.remarks: Both games write their graphs in the same named stream (); they differ in where a graph under a model stands, which the placing game has already settled. The nodes carry no light or terrain flag: Project I.G.I.'s graphs author neither. Materials need no translation, the two games' game materials sharing their rows.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiGraph.UpdateCover(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.IIgi2CollisionQuery)
member.summary: Works the graph's cover out from the world about it, as the client does for a graph flagged to update it (AIGraph_UpdateNodeCover, igi2 0x5B7BE0 per node): what the level ships is replaced.

remarks.para: From each node, raised to each of the four , a line runs out in each of 32 directions round it, the first due east and the rest turning left; a line that meets something shelters the node from that way at that height, a bit of its direction's word, the lowest for the lowest height.

A node is cover only where it is sheltered from at least three directions low down (one of the three lower heights) but open at the top, so a soldier crouched there hides and stood up sees over: a node walled in to head height is not cover.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2AiPathSearch
member.summary: A soldier's A* search over a graph, AIGraphAStarSearchData_s (aigraph.c): it may run over several ticks, a number of nodes a call, and keeps the path it found until it is cleared.

remarks.para: The open list is kept sorted by estimated total cost, a new node going after those that cost no more. A link's cost is its length, 81920 more where it joins a vehicle node to a node that is not one, plus the weight of the node it leads to; the estimate is the straight distance to the destination. A node reached again more cheaply, open or closed, is moved back into the open list.

Called again for the same graph, source and destination, the search resumes where it stopped. Once the path is built the open and closed lists are let go, so a call after that finds nothing to search and fails, as the original's does: a caller asks for the path first.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Igi2HumanSoldierTask
member.summary: An enemy soldier's body as level data places it, I.G.I. 2's HumanSoldier.

remarks.para: Its parameters are the Human ones it inherits; its HumanAI is a child.

It is the task the engine's weapon and explosion events are sent to, as retail's HumanSoldier is: the port keeps the soldier's state on its , which answers them. Before the body is made it stops no round and takes nothing.

member.content: Its save state, HumanSoldier_ptSerializeParameterList: a human's, then the state that last set its main animation, which squads have seen it dead and whether a camera has. Those three are not kept here, so they are written as a new soldier has them.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2AiContent
member.content: The simple actions: waits, looks, moves, sounds and the dead.
The standing and fighting actions: idle, combat idle, offensive and defensive combat, the grenade, standing fire and the mounted gun.

What each action keeps between ticks, the members of HumanAIActionContext_t's union an action reads: each class holds one action's fields, named for what they are rather than for the union member the C reaches them through.
member.summary: The soldiers' actions, humanaicontent.c: each action's callbacks (its Init, Run, Delete and the sub-behaviours it runs inside itself), the orders a squad gives, and the firing they share.
member.remarks: An action is recognised by its Init, as the original compares pfInitCallback; the callbacks are static methods so that two delegates made from one compare equal.
member.content: The using and walking-about actions: activating, the patrol, taking cover and the rough look.
The squad's orders as a member carries them out: formation, inquiry, the move to a node and the leapfrog wait.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2AiSquad
member.summary: A squad's mind, I.G.I. 2's AISquad_s at run time: its soldiers' minds in up to two teams, the events its members report (which its script handles), the enemies they share, a stack of up to four squad actions, and the timers that keep it tense.

remarks.para: AISquad_RunHandler counts its members, lets finished lines go and, while any live, keeps an action running, fires its rotating fire order, ages its targets, keeps the members' combat idle, hands the events to the top action (whose handler runs the script), runs that action, and finally runs its soldiers. A squad with no members left only runs its soldiers.
The original numbers its formation tick from the squad's heap address; this port numbers it from the squad's task id, which is as arbitrary and stays the same from run to run.

member.content: Its save state, AISquad_ptSerializeParameterList (aisquad.c): whether it is dead, its flags, its timers and suspicion, and its actions.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2AiWorld.EvaluateGunShot(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2GunShot,System.Object)
member.summary: Every human weighs a shot's bullets before they fly, human.c Human_EvaluateGunShotHandler: a soldier with a mind hears the bullets that pass within two metres of its head, one event each.
member.param: Who holds the weapon that made it.

remarks.para: The shot's creator is the weapon itself (Weapon_CreateHandler), never a human, so the handler's test of the creator's team always compares with team one: a human of team one hears nothing, whoever fired. A human holding the shot's creator would be skipped, but none does.

Retail's quirk is kept too: the n-th event is told of the n-th bullet of the shot, from its muzzle, whichever bullets were the ones heard. The event's originator is the shot's ignored task, a mounted gun's holder, and its team; with none, team nought.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2HumanAi
member.summary: An enemy soldier's mind, I.G.I. 2's HumanAI (humanai.c): it hears events, runs its script on the most important kind, keeps a stack of actions and runs the top one, looks for enemies, and writes the channels that drive its body.

remarks.para: A tick (, HumanAI_RunHandler): the idle sweep of the view, the sector it stands in, the animation speed, timers, whether it sees a target, its queued lines, its alert state, which view it uses, where its eyes are; then, once its script and graph are there, on the first tick its creation event, after that its death checks and an idle event when it has nothing to do; then its script, its top action and its detection; last, its channels go to its body and are cleared.

member.content: What a mind sees and how it looks (HumanAI_RunDetection, the views, the targets).
The footing a mind gives its soldier from the graph, human.c Human_GroundCollision (its HumanAI half).
How a mind aims its soldier's grenade, HumanAI_GetGrenadeOrientationAndSpeedToTarget (igi2 0x4632A0).
How a mind walks its soldier along the graph and turns it (HumanAI_MoveCharacter*, HumanAI_Face*).

Its save state, HumanAI_ptSerializeParameterList (humanai.c): its flags, whether it has yet to run, its visibility timer, its nodes, its legal nodes, and its patrols, each by its command's, last end's and path's level ids. Its detection, events, actions, search and movement are not kept; HumanAI_DeSerializeHandler starts them afresh and sends a patrolling soldier on again.
A mind's state between ticks: nodes, timers, lines to say (tCommon, tCombat and the scalars).
The helpers the actions and squads ask of a mind.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2HumanAi.RunDetection
member.summary: A tick of perception (HumanAI_RunDetection): the detection view is built from the head, turned by the idle sweep and, while aiming, toward the target; detection runs; each enemy listed is identified over a delay that grows with distance and gloom (and on easier difficulties), and raises AIEVENT_ENEMYDETECTION (or _NO_LOF when no bone it sees can be shot through) once confirmed, AIEVENT_SEENSOMETHING before; a dead friend seen raises AIEVENT_FRIENDLYDETECTION. Then the target position follows the target, or with none the weapon is reloaded under nine tenths and, unless the squad shares a target, the target is forgotten after ten seconds.

remarks.para: The stretch runs from the node the soldier stands on to the node beside it: the first step of its way ahead, or, between legal nodes, whichever of the two it does not stand on. With no legal nodes the stretch may instead run back to the node it came from, when that node lies nearer the soldier than the node it stands on does.

The footing lies under where the move started, at the stretch's height that far along it; its normal is straight up and its material is the standing node's. The light is the standing node's and the next one's, mixed by the same fraction, even when the stretch was turned back.

The first throw whose flight meets nothing on its way () is the throw; the orientation is level.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Ai.Runtime.Igi2HumanAiNatives
member.summary: The soldier script's natives, AIAction_* and AIFunction_* as HumanAI_RegisterScriptFunctions registers them: each works on the mind whose script is running (HumanAI_ptCurrentHumanAI) and the event it runs for.

remarks.para: An AIAction_* asks for an action: it takes a state for it, fills the state from its arguments and the event, and lists the action for the mind to push once the script is done (HumanAI_AddActionToLocalList), at the rank the script runs at. Its last argument is always the action's flags, bit 1 making it pushable. With no state free the action is not asked for.

An AIFunction_Set* tuning value is scaled as the original stores it: seconds to ticks (30), metres to world units (4096), per cent to a share, degrees to radians. The accuracy setters recompute the factors the accuracy curve is drawn with.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Animation.Igi2AnimationLibrary
member.summary: Every clip a level has loaded, filed by the rig it was authored on and by its own name: the hierarchy table (Hierarchy_ptHashTable) the engine looks animations up in.

remarks.para: A rig is identified by the shape of its tree alone, the child-count bytes of its hierarchy (Hierarchy_Compare, igi2 0x57EBB0), so every model and every clip that shares a skeleton shares one table. A bone model registers its rig as its pack's models load (MTP_ModelLoad, 0x4F4F00); a clip registers under its header's name with the rig it carries (Hierarchy_LoadAnim, 0x57F060), and is dropped when no model has registered that rig yet.

Each pack loads its models and then the clips its BANM chunk names, LOCAL:anims/<name>.iff (MTP_ParseMTP, 0x4F5DE0), packs in load order. A name is compared exactly, case and all, and the first clip registered under a name is the one found (a chained table appending at the tail and searching from the head).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Animation.Igi2AnimBlend
member.summary: A blend from one pose source to another, AnimBlender_t: its timing and the pose it mixes.

remarks.para: AnimBlender_Blend (igi2 0x5D9DB0) starts it from an old source to a new one over a length in clip ticks, finished at once if that is nought; each run (AnimBlender_RunHandler, 0x5D9630) adds a frame's 160 ticks while it is short of its length, and on the run after it reaches it the blend is finished. A blender that drops its old source (bit 1 of its flags) takes that source's clip away once it finishes.

Its pose (AnimBlender_InterpolateHandler, 0x5D9780): with no clip on the new source, every masked bone is the identity. Finished, the old source writes only the bones the new one does not animate and then the new one writes its own, straight into the bones it was handed. Blending, both write into working buffers of their own and each masked bone is slerped from the old to the new, or taken from whichever animates it alone; the root translation is mixed the same way.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Animation.Igi2AnimController
member.summary: One clip being played: its time, its step a tick and whether it has ended, AnimController_t.

remarks.para: AnimController_SetAnimationAndTime (igi2 0x554850) sets a clip, takes the loop flag from it, resets the step to one frame's worth of ticks, and moves to the time asked for, wrapped into the clip one tick beyond its end; the ended bit is cleared afterwards, even when that time is the end. AnimController_Step (0x5549A0) moves to a time: one at or beyond the end, or before the start, sets the ended bit and then wraps for a looping clip or stops at that end for any other. The ended bit stays set once a looping clip has wrapped, until a clip is set again.

A step fires the clip's anim triggers it plays through (AnimController_TriggerEvents, 0x553D50), on its : forward, those after the old time up to the new; backward, those after the new time up to the old, still in time order. A looping clip that wraps forward first fires the rest of the clip and then the start up to the new time; wrapping backward, the start up to the old time and then the rest after the new. A clip set afresh fires the triggers at the tick it is set to and the one before (AnimController_Seek, 0x553F60, fires none and leaves the time one before). A controller with fires none.

The clip's other events, its attach objects and the interpolated pose are not run here. A trigger placed on a bone fires only for a bone the controller animates; this takes every bone of the clip as animated, which holds for a controller playing the whole body.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Animation.Igi2BoneSkin
member.summary: A boned model's vertices as the sequel's renderer rebuilds them on load, and their posing on a skeleton.

remarks.para: The file keeps I.G.I. 1's layout, a base vertex per point on its one bone and then extra weighted influences that name a base vertex, but the sequel does not skin it that way. On load (Direct3DRender_CreateBoneRenderMesh, igi2ed 0x56A400) every base vertex is moved from its bone's frame into the model's rest frame by its bone's bind position, and gets up to four bone slots: its own bone with its +32 float turned into a weight byte, then one slot for each extra influence that names it. A fifth influence takes the slot of the lightest one when it is no lighter, and is dropped otherwise. An extra influence's own position is never read.
The bind positions are the hierarchy's translations summed down from the root (Direct3DRender_SetBoneTranslations, 0x56A750): the rest pose has no rotation.

Posing is Direct3DRender_ProcessVerticesBone (0x568BE0) as the nearest detail draws it: each slot places the vertex by its bone, from the vertex less that bone's bind position, and the results are summed by weight. Every slot but the last weighs its byte over 255; the last takes what is left of one. The normal is turned by the first slot's bone alone. The first-person view always draws at that detail (Direct3DRender_DrawBoneMesh, 0x56FC30, forces it on layer zero). A face's morph targets move the rest positions by their weights first (Direct3DRender_MorphVerticesBone).

member.summary: The clips a weapon type gives a body, one per base animation: WeaponTypeAnim_MakeAnimTable (igi2 0x4F9CA0) over the base names WeaponTypeAnim_InitBaseAnimNameTable (0x4F7940) sets.

remarks.para: A state names a base animation by index (a human's state-animation table); the weapon it holds turns that into a clip. For each base name the table tries, on the body's rig: the base name, an underscore and the weapon's own animation name, lower-cased (stand_ak47); then the base name and the weapon's family (stand_rifle); then the base name alone; then stand_lowerbody. Only the first is lower-cased, so a clip whose name has a capital in it is never found by the first attempt.
Several slots share a name, and two are left empty (they are never assigned and find nothing).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Audio.Igi2AmbientAreaTask
member.summary: A box of ambient sound, I.G.I. 2's AmbientArea (ambientarea.c): while the listener is within it (or within its falloff), one of its sounds at a time plays at the listener, at a volume that fades in and out, with a drawn pause between sounds.

remarks.para: AmbientArea_RunHandler: unless its On expression fails, the listener's offset is turned into the box's frame and measured in metres: outside the size plus the falloff the target volume is nought; inside the size it is one; between, one less the distance past the size over the falloff. The area counts only where the listener's place allows it (inside a building or out). The volume steps toward the target, up while the area counts and down otherwise, by one over the fade time in ticks plus one, and never above the target. At nought the sound stops and a new pause is drawn; while a sound plays its volume follows; with none playing, a sound of the list is drawn every tick the area counts, and started once the pause is spent. The pause counts down every tick. Its children run under it.
Its Noise level, when above nought, lists it with the areas that muffle what soldiers hear (AmbientArea_GetNoiseLevelAtPosition).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Audio.Igi2SoundDefinitions
member.summary: The level's sound definitions: what every name game code says resolves to, SoundSys_ptSoundDefQTaskList as Game_CreateHandler (igi2 0x4070E0) fills it.

remarks.para: Three scripts, one after the other, each the sounds script of a directory (SoundSys_NewSoundDefParentQTask, 0x42EEB0): the game's own under LOCAL:common/sounds/, the location's under its common directory, then the mission's under MISSION:sounds/. Every one is made of calls to four natives, DefineGroup, DefineSound, DefineGraph and DefineTriggerOnce, and of nothing else but TRUE and FALSE, so they are run in a namespace of those six.

The dedicated server's natives parse nothing (SoundDefSound_ScriptParseCB, 0x57C540, returns at once) and its sound is never switched on, so the arguments are read as the editor reads them (igi2ed 0x430B70, 0x4349C0, 0x434B20, 0x435A10). They are I.G.I.'s arguments in I.G.I.'s order, with one rule of I.G.I. 2's own: a sound whose nearest distance is nought hears at full volume to a fiftieth of its farthest.

A name is found as SoundSys_NewSoundFn (0x42F6F0) finds it: each script's definitions in turn, a group answering to its own name before any inside it (SoundDefGroup_FindSoundDefHandler, igi2ed 0x434580), strcmp and the first match wins.

member.summary: The level's sounds: the ones SoundSys_NewSoundFn (igi2 0x42F6F0) makes, each following what it hangs off.

remarks.para: Whether a sound is made is the definitions' answer alone: there is one for every name they define, whatever the mixer does with it, so the game decides the same whether or not anything is heard. Retail's own answer differs only when it has no sound at all (SoundSys_isSoundDisabled), which a played game never is.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2BoneTrace
member.summary: Lines against a boned object's posed mesh, BoneDynCubeObj_TraceLinesHandler (igi2 0x5655A0), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: The trace's evaluate event is asked first, then each line in turn: a line that misses the object's sphere (BoneDynCubeObj_SphereIntersectionCheck, 0x565180) is passed over. When the first line reaches it, every vertex is placed once by its bone and then turned by the object's orientation rows. Each line is taken relative to the object's position, unturned; a box padded by a centimetre around it culls the faces, which are all tested in order, the sphere tree unused, with the shared plane and barycentric test and tie window ().

A hit records the struck point, the face's normal (normalised; the vertices were turned, so it is the world's), its turn back by the orientation's columns as the local normal, the face and material, a light of one, and the bone: the first vertex's, or the second's when the second and third share one the first does not. Portals and an ignored material are not tested for.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2BoneLineOfSight
member.summary: A line of sight against a boned object's posed mesh, BoneDynCubeObj_LineOfSightHandler (igi2 0x566B90), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: The bones are brought up to date, then the line's evaluate event is asked, then the line must come within the object's sphere (). Every vertex of the first mesh level is placed by its bone alone: unlike the trace, the object's orientation is not applied, so the mesh stands as if the object faced along the world's axes. The line is taken relative to the object's position; a box padded by 40.96 around it culls the faces, which are all tested in order.

A face is crossed where the line meets its plane within the line, and within the face by the two coordinates of the plane's strongest axes. Each crossing marks the line crossed; one entered from the front lets through its material's share of what is left. A face of no material, or of one that lets nothing through, stops the line and this object. Unlike a solid model's, a boned object leaves the nearest material and its distance as they were.
A human answers a line with no evaluate event through this handler too (Human_LineOfSightHandler, 0x4FF1E0), except its own first-person view's body, which only the player has.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2CollisionWorld
member.summary: The level as the collision engine sees it: every placed solid model and the ground, and the queries that trace lines through them.

remarks.para: The original keeps its objects in two octrees, a stationary one and one for things that move. The queries a body uses to find its footing read only the stationary tree. Every type that answers such a query is a RigidDynCubeObj or derives from one: EditRigidObj, Door, Switch, Lift, Building and its sectors, and the RigidMagicObjs a model's attachments become. They all answer with one handler, . Bone models answer line traces but not ground queries, and characters are in the moving tree.

The octree decides only which handlers are called. Each handler then tests its own bounds, so a linear walk over a sphere test finds the same surfaces. What it can change is the order, and with it which of two surfaces at exactly the same distance a line keeps: a handler replaces a hit only when it is strictly nearer.

remarks.para: Every static placement becomes an object at the pose its parameters give through , and so does every model its model attaches, recursively. That is ModelObj_CreateAttachObject (igi2 0x56D0B0): an attachment's name is looked up in the magic table (), which gives the model it wears; a name it does not hold is used as a model; a shadow volume or a mark is no solid.
A model with bones becomes a BoneMagicObj, which does not answer ground queries, so it is left out. Its own attachments are still followed.
A straight spline segment becomes an , its radius taken over the model's levels of detail; one bent along its curve has its meshes bent along it ().

remarks.para: The objects of the stationary tree along the line answer first, each with its own handler: the solid models (), the spline segments () and the stands of trees () and the boned bodies (); a line of no length meets none. Then, if anything still gets through and the ground is asked for, the line is traced against the ground alone, and striking it blocks the sight.

The original walks its octree's cubes along the line. Each handler tests its own bounds, so a walk over every object meets the same faces; only the order can differ, and with it which of two materials crossed at exactly the same distance is kept.

member.summary: A stand of trees as lines meet it: the stand's index walked toward the lines, and each tree near them traced as a solid model placed where the tree stands.

remarks.para: The original keeps one solid model in the stand, tRigidTree, moves it onto each tree it tests, and runs the solid model's own line handler on it. A hit by the tree is then reported as a hit on the stand.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2RigidLineOfSight
member.summary: A line of sight against a placed solid model: RigidDynCubeObj_LineOfSightHandler (igi2 0x58CCA0), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: The trace's search () with its own sums: the line into the model's frame, a box around it with no pad, the same sphere-tree walk summing every node alike, and the same face test with the plane's products summed x, z, y. Portal faces are never met, nor is a model once the sight has been stopped.

Every face the line crosses counts, not only the nearest: each marks the line crossed, keeps the nearer material, and lets through its material's transparency when entered from the front; a face of no material, or of one that lets nothing through, stops the line and the search.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2RigidTrace
member.summary: Lines against a placed solid model: RigidDynCubeObj_TraceLinesHandler (igi2 0x58B3B0), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: The same search as the first game's model ray (): each line is taken into the model's frame, a padded box around it culls the sphere tree and the faces, and each face is met with a plane test and a barycentric test on the face's dominant axis. A face a little behind the best is still taken if it faces the line and the best does not, so a line through two coincident faces reports the one it enters.

What the sequel changed: the box pad and the tie window are 40.96 units (one centimetre) where the first game used a tenth of a unit; portal faces stop a line only when asked, and then only from their front; one material row can be ignored; a hit reports its barycentric position and how lit the surface is; and every operation rounds to 24 bits, toward zero. The order of each sum and where each value is stored as a float are the disassembly's. The walk and the face test are shared with the spline segments' handler ().

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2SplineSegment
member.content: A segment bent along its curve, SplineObjSegment with its linear flag clear: its collision meshes are bent once, when it is made, into the segment's own space, and lines are traced against them there.

remarks.para: SplineObjSegment_TransformVertex (igi2 0x5BA740) takes a model vertex's X as a place along the curve: from the model's X extent onto the segment's areas, which picks an area and a fraction into it. The vertex's Y and Z are an offset in the area's cross-section, turned by the area's frame and added to the area's point, at each end of the area; the two are mixed by the fraction. A flipped segment runs the extent the other way.

The sphere tree is the model's, its centres bent the same way (SplineObjSegment_TransformSpherePos, 0x5B7140), and each radius grown again to reach every vertex of every face beneath it (SplineObjSegment_CreateSphere, 0x5BA4F0).
The areas' points and frames are the curve's samples (), taken from the segment's midpoint.

member.summary: A straight spline segment, SplineObjSegment with its linear flag set, as the collision sees it: the segment model stretched from one waypoint to the next.

remarks.para: SplineObjSegment_Update (igi2 0x5BAB10) places the segment at the midpoint of its two waypoints and builds one matrix that takes the model's own frame to the world's: its first column is the chord between the waypoints over the model's X extent, its other two the chord's turn about the vertical. The model's X is measured from the middle of that extent. The handler traces the model's own collision mesh, unbent, by taking each line into that frame with the matrix's inverse.
Every value is formed as the client's 24-bit truncating FPU forms it — the midpoint too, so a waypoint far from the origin puts the segment a quarter unit or so off the true middle.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2SplineSegmentLineOfSight
member.summary: A line of sight against a straight spline segment: SplineObjSegment_LineOfSightHandler (igi2 0x5B9E70), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: Unlike the solid models, a segment answers sight with its line trace (), cast again and again: each cast starts 40.96 units past the last face it struck, so every face along the line is met in turn. A sight already crossed elsewhere starts its first cast past that crossing.

Only a face entered from the front, with a material, counts: it marks the sight crossed, becomes its material and where it was crossed, and lets through its material's transparency. The casts stop when the line runs clear, when a face lets nothing more through, or, on a sight crossed before, at a face no nearer than the last once nothing gets through.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2SplineSegmentTrace
member.summary: Lines against a straight spline segment: the linear path of SplineObjSegment_TraceLinesHandler (igi2 0x5B7390), with the arithmetic the client's FPU performs.

remarks.para: The handler answers both the line and the ground events. Each line is taken into the segment model's own frame by the inverse of the stretch matrix and walked through the model's own sphere tree and faces, the walk and face test the solid models use () with this handler's sums: every sphere sums its squared distance x, y, z, and the plane distance sums z, y, x. Portal faces and the ignored material are not consulted.

A hit is taken back into the world by the stretch matrix and measured from the line's start there; its normal is the struck face's edges stretched, crossed and normalised, reversed on a flipped segment. Every hit reports a double face, and the sector, portal and barycentric fields are left as they were.

Two things are kept that look like slips. An earlier hit is taken into the model's frame by the stretch matrix's transpose rather than its inverse, and from the segment's position rather than the stretch's middle, so the box it shortens and the distance a face must beat are only roughly where that hit is. And a line whose bounds miss the segment ends the whole call, not just that line.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.Igi2TerrainLineTrace
member.summary: Lines in any direction against the ground: Terrain_TraceLinesHandler1 (igi2 0x5730B0), with the client's FPU arithmetic.

remarks.para: Every tile is walked for every line, in the tiles' declared order. The line is taken into the tile's sample grid, clipped to it, and stepped along its longer axis a column (or row) at a time; each step tests the cell the line is in and, where it crosses into the next row, that cell too. A cell is two triangles split along its flatter diagonal, and the first of them the line crosses nearer than anything found so far, outside the discard boxes, is the tile's hit.

A tile's hit replaces the line's result only when nearer, and only when no later tile owns the point: the last tile in declared order whose interior, half a sample in from its edges, holds the point is the only one whose hit counts there, so a finer tile laid over a coarser one answers for the ground it covers.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Computer.Igi2ComputerHilightTask
member.summary: A mark on the map computer, I.G.I. 2's ComputerHilight (computerhilight.c): the placed tasks it draws, or else a sprite at its position, with a marker, two texts and the objective it belongs to.

remarks.para: Its TaskID text names up to 64 tasks, as numbers or ranges written a-b (ComputerHilight_ExtractTaskID); its marker mesh and colour are one-line scripts naming MARKER_* constants. ComputerHilight_RunHandler: while it has a Hilight expression, it is shown as that expression's value; one with none is shown only once an objective sets its sprite (ComputerHilight_SetSprite).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Config.Igi2GameConfig
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's configuration, Config_tConfig (config.c): the player profiles, which is active, and the graphics options in force, read at start-up from config.qvm (Config_LoadConfig).

remarks.para: The file is a compiled script of GO* calls: GOVersion, GOStart (the active profile), GOContentControlPW, then for each profile GOPlayer and its settings, and GOComplete at the end. A file that never reaches GOComplete is not taken: the defaults stand (Config_DefaultGameOptions). A file older than version five enables BreakScript, which stops it.
The GfxOptions_* calls set the options in force; GfxOptions_ApplyCurrentOptionsToLastPlayerProfile files them with the profile just read.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Detection.Igi2HostPlayerVisibility
member.summary: How well I.G.I. 2's soldiers see a player of the game hosting them: I.G.I. 2's own measure of its player (), worked out for the host's player each tick.

remarks.para: I.G.I. 2's detectors see a human only as far as its visibility factor times their cone's length (AIDetection_RunDetection), and its player's factor is never one. A host's player is measured by nothing of the kind, so without this it would be seen at a cone's full length: a soldier 70 metres off opens fire as a level starts.

The light is what the host's level bakes under the feet, its layers asked in turn (), else the tuning's. Moving is read from how far the feet go in a tick, since the host's player has no I.G.I. 2 locomotion; turning on the spot is not seen through the body. A loud shot is one of the player's own gunshots that reaches further than I.G.I. 2's loud range, heard as the host's level broadcasts it.

member.param: The host level's baked light, its layers in the order they are asked.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2AreaActivateTask
member.summary: A box that counts what is inside it, I.G.I. 2's AreaActivate, exporting nActive and nClientID.

remarks.para: Its tick (AreaActivateQTask_RunHandler, igi2 0x592FC0): each criterion its mask names counts what it answers for inside, in the criteria's order, and the sum is nActive unless detection is off; then its children run.
A point is inside (AreaActivateQTask_IsInsideArea, 0x593190) when, taken from the box's centre into its frame, it is within half the box's dimensions along each axis, edges included.

A team's criterion counts every human of a team in the mask, the dead too unless an AI drives them (Human_AreaActivateTeamCB, 0x5007E0); each team bit the mask holds runs it again, so a mask of two teams counts each human twice. CRITERIA_HUMAN counts the active (Human_AreaActivateAllHumansCB, 0x500910); CRITERIA_HUMANPLAYER the level's task 0 when it is the player (HumanPlayer_AreaActivateCB, 0x49E290). CRITERIA_CAMERA counts the game screen's camera (GameScreen_CameraInAreaCB), CRITERIA_VEHICLE each car at its position (Vehicle_AeraActivateCB, the list Car_CreateHandler registers in), and CRITERIA_HUMANAI_SIDEKICK each human whose mind is a side-kick's, dead or alive (HumanAI_AreaActivateSideKickCB).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2CutSceneTask
member.summary: A cutscene, I.G.I. 2's CutScene: its clock and its end, exporting isRun, isFinished and nTick.

remarks.para: CutScene_RunHandler (igi2 0x43A470): its children run, then its Run script says whether it runs (it does when there is none), which every running cutscene adds to CutScene_isRunning; its Reset script, when it holds, winds it back to its start. While it runs its cameras are placed for the tick (CutScene_SetCamera, 0x439F20) and its clock advances: by the Time delta script's seconds when there is one, never below nought, else by a tick. Its Start expression runs the tick it starts and its Stop expression the tick it stops.

It ends when its time passes the sum of its cameras' durations, each scaled by its time scale and summed in the FPU's chopped single precision; it then holds its clock at the end. One with no cameras never ends.

Its camera for the tick (CutScene_InterpolateCamera, 0x438F10) is its four cameras about the time, the one on and its neighbours (a camera that is not smoothed to the next stands in for the one after it): every value interpolated between them, its frame from the angles; a camera looking at a target turned to it; letterboxed by its fades; and shaken by the shake's random stream. It is what the level shows while the cutscene runs. Its filters are its presentation's, and a camera's link (EditCamera_TransformRelativeToLinkQTask, 0x5815E0), which no mission 1 camera uses, is not ported.
It is made as though it ran last (CutScene_CreateHandler, 0x43A0E0): one running from its first tick does not run its start expression, and one that is not runs its stop expression once.

member.content: Its save state, CutScene_ptSerializeParameterList: whether it runs and has finished, and its clock.

member.summary: A countdown on screen, I.G.I. 2's MissionTimer (missiontimer.c): it starts when its start expression holds, counts its time down a tick at a time except while its pause expression holds, and shows minutes and seconds until it runs out.

remarks.para: MissionTimer_UpdateInternalDataHandler: the ticks left are its seconds times thirty, chopped. MissionTimer_RunHandler: waiting, a start expression that holds sets it running and puts its display on the screen; running, unless a pause expression holds, it loses a tick, and with none left it is finished and its display goes.
MissionTimerDrawTask_DrawHandler: MM : SS in font3, its minutes the ticks over 1800 and its seconds the rest over thirty, centred at half the screen's width and nine tenths of its height.

member.summary: A line said to the player, I.G.I. 2's StatusMessage: once its script sends it, its sound plays and its text is shown a piece at a time on the status message screen, exporting isSendt, nTickSendt, isFinishedDisplay, nFinishedDisplay and nTicksSinceFinishedDisplay.

remarks.para: Its text is a list of keys, each a piece shown in turn: split at a comma, a tab or a line's end, a // commenting out the rest of a line, each key looked up in the language (StatusMessage_UpdateText, igi2 0x50F830). Its duration is shared out among the pieces by their length (StatusMessage_InitText, 0x50F9A0); a sound it finds replaces the duration with the sound's own length (StatusMessage_PlaySound, 0x50F750).

Its tick (StatusMessage_RunHandler, 0x50FB30): once sent it is shown, each piece registered on the screen in turn as the last one's share of the duration runs out; when the last is out and the screen has finished printing it, the line ends, its sound is cut, and it counts as finished display. One sent once is then done; another may be sent again. Its children run every tick.
A line with no text is never put on the screen and so never finishes: its sound plays out, it stays sent and shown, and its clock restarts each time its duration is out, as retail's does.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2LevelRun
member.summary: The level's tick: its task tree run from the root, every task by its own run handler, as Flow_RunChildren (igi2 0x401A50) runs the game's tasks.

remarks.para: The run pass is not a walk of the tree. A task's children run only if its run handler runs them, as Container's does (Container_RunHandler, 0x5C6C60) and as a ConditionalContainer's does only while its condition holds; a type with no run handler stops the pass beneath it.

The root is the Level (Level_LevelRunHandler, 0x543400), which runs its children and then counts the tick. Its Static child does nothing (Level_StaticRunHandler, 0x5434A0); its Dynamic child (Level_DynamicRunHandler, 0x5435F0) runs the level's own objects, then what has been added after them — grenades, explosions and what they leave () — then the delayed pass (RunDelayed_Run, 0x58FDB0).

A task whose behaviour lives outside the tree, the player's, is bound to its node () and runs there, in the tree's order and under its containers' conditions. The tick rate is the shared , GAME_FREQUENCY.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2MissionScoreSettingsTask.GetRank(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2MissionScore@,System.Boolean[])
member.summary: The highest rank a mission earned, -1 for none (MissionScoreSettings_GetRank): from IGI Operative down, the first rank whose every requirement is met. A requirement is skipped when rank nought's value for it is below nought (retail reads rank nought's for every rank); the time required is at least the seconds taken, the spotted limit at least the times spotted, the health required at most the health left, and the accuracy required at most the hits per hundred rounds fired (met with none fired). Loads are not checked. A mission that took no time earns none.
member.param: Receives, for the last rank weighed, which of the five items were met.

member.summary: One step of a sequence of scripts, I.G.I. 2's SequenceCommand.

remarks.para: The sequences under a task are its SequenceCommand children, and only the first of them drives (SequenceCommand_RunHandler, igi2 0x492080): unless it has been stopped, each tick it runs the step it is on — itself, when it is on none or the one it was on is gone — with SequenceCommand_SetCommand pointed at it.

A step (SequenceCommand_RunSequenceCommandHandler, 0x491F70): when its IsRun Expression holds, its Run Expression runs, and then when its IsNext Expression holds its Next Expression runs — which is where a step names the one after it.

member.content: Its save state, SoundGenerator_ptSerializeParameterList: its sound, and whether it plays.
member.summary: A sound the level's scripts start and stop where the object it hangs off stands, I.G.I. 2's SoundGenerator, exporting isPlaying.

remarks.para: It declares no parameters: what it plays is whatever its children's scripts last asked for. SoundGenerator_RunHandler (igi2 0x486C90) points SoundGenerator_PlaySound and SoundGenerator_StopSound at itself, runs its children — the SequenceCommands that call them — and lets the two natives go again.

SoundGenerator_PlaySound (0x486950) deletes the sound it has, takes the new name and makes the sound, and is playing only when one was made; SoundGenerator_StopSound (0x486910) deletes it. Neither notices a sound ending on its own, so isPlaying stays set after a one-shot has finished.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2StatusMessageScreen
member.summary: Where the status messages are printed, I.G.I. 2's StatusMessageScreen: twenty-four places, each a line printed a letter at a time, which tells its message when it is done printing.

remarks.para: A message registers into the first free place (StatusMessageScreen_RegisterMessage, igi2 0x43D8A0) and is unprinted again; a line that is not a cutscene's is also kept in the computer's log, and starts printing from its first letter, a cutscene's from its end.

Each tick (StatusMessageScreen_UpdateMessage, 0x43D540), unless the game is paused: a cutscene's line is laid out whole and counts as done; another's box opens over two ticks and fades in over seven, and from its ninth tick a letter is printed every other tick until the line is out, after which it counts as done. Thirty ticks of done, and its message is told it has finished printing, which is what lets a message end.
The screen is a game screen's, which runs after the level each tick.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2Strings
member.summary: The game's localised text, Config_GetLocalizedStringForLanguage (igi2 0x424BD0): a key is a resource, looked up first as GLOBAL: and then under the language's own folder, and a key nothing holds is its own text.

remarks.para: The strings come from the language's archives the screens load: LANGUAGE:messages.res, the status messages' (StatusMessageScreen_LoadResource, 0x43DC40), and LANGUAGE:objectives.res, the computer's (ComputerMenu_LoadComputerMenuResource, 0x532CD0). Each names its strings LOCAL:english/<key>.

Unlike the menus' table, which shows a missing key marked, the game shows it as it is written: retail remembers the key as a missing resource whose text is the key, so "Quicksave done", which no archive holds, reads as itself.

member.param: The registry the archives were registered into.
The language's name, Config_azGameLanguage's entry; by default the one the player has chosen now.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human
member.content: A human as the areas count it.
Riding something: a human held to a ladder or a mounted gun goes where that thing carries it and faces as it turns (human.c Human_AttachToTask, Human_Attach, Human_DetachFromTask).
member.summary: Blood: the spurt where a round enters flesh and the stains it leaves, HumanDamage_CreateFleshEnterEffect.
member.content: The body's bones as its clips pose them, the collision that follows them, and the zone a hit finds on them.
member.summary: A human body, as I.G.I. 2's Human_s keeps it: the part the player and the soldiers share.

remarks.para: The channel block that drives it, the locomotion state machine, the posture, the speeds the body moves by, its damage and its death — and the Human_* functions that work on them whoever the human is. What only the player has (its tuning, its input, its action machine and its own states) lives in the derived class.

member.summary: A dead body coming to rest: it falls, is pushed out of what its limbs sink into, slides to a stop and lies along the ground (Human_HandleDeathCollision, Human_CheckBoneCollision, Human_InterpolateZAxisToAveragedGroundNormal).
member.content: A human as detectors see it, Human_AIDetectionGetInfoHandler for the player and soldiers alike.
member.summary: The eyes: where the view sits on the body, and which way it looks.
member.content: The sounds a human's own clips make: its footsteps and its body's fall.
member.summary: The ground under a human: what it stands on, how far below its feet, and the roof above its head.
member.content: Where a human's body and the weapon in its hand stand, for what it drops.
The pain a human cries out when hurt.
member.summary: Keeping out of other humans, Human_HumanCollision.
The move: the speeds a body is integrated by, and the platform it rides.
member.content: Telling the level's listeners where the human is, human.c Human_Notify.
Putting a body somewhere at once, rather than moving it there.
The shared human's run handler.

Its save state, Human_ptSerializeParameterList (human.c): a model object's, then its channels as they were and are, its damage, its flags, its pose, camera and timers, its angles, its speeds, its distances to the ground and roof, its mission's figures, its state machine (Human_ptSerializeStateParameterList), and what it stands on.
Whether a bullet may strike the body.
member.summary: The body's turn: its angles, and the orientation built from them.
member.content: Whether a lying body has room to turn (human.c Human_IsGammaRotationAllowed).
member.summary: The walls around a human: the sweep that keeps a move out of them and the ceiling that limits a posture.
The human as its weapon sees it: the parent the Weapon task asks, and the fields a shot touches.

member.summary: Blood where a round goes into the body: a stain on what lies three metres beyond the wound, a mist at the wound, a cone of drops thrown forward along the round and a wider spray thrown back, HumanDamage_CreateFleshEnterEffect.
member.param: The human hurt, whose light tints the mist; when no human was.

remarks.para: Nothing happens with blood turned off in the options. Otherwise the run stream is drawn from: for a stain, the size and which of two textures (only when the line beyond the wound ends in a material whose bullets leave a penetrating hole); then a count of 12 to 14 drops forward and one draw for each one's spin; then 16 to 18 drops back, and a draw each. The drops' directions come from the particle module's own stream.
Each human keeps one mist and one spray system, made anew once the last has burnt out. The spray's drops leave stains where they land ().

member.summary: Moves a dead body: it counts its ticks near the ground, and until it lies still it falls, is pushed out by its limbs, loses the part of its speed that drove it into them, stops sliding when slow and slides with friction on the ground (Human_HandleDeathCollision).

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.CheckBoneCollision
member.summary: Traces the dead body's limbs, from 0.2 m above its lower back to each limb's bone as it will be after this tick's speed, and sums how far out of what they sink into each would be pushed (Human_CheckBoneCollision).
member.remarks: Fourteen lines: the eleven limbs; one 0.35 m straight down from the lower back and one three metres down (traced, but its push not counted); and one fifteen metres up from the feet. Only surfaces facing no more than sixty degrees down count. Each counted line pushes back along the surface's normal by how far its end lies beyond it; the legs, toes and the short line below the back hold the body up by the most any of them asks. With more than one push, the sideways push is their mean.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.UpdateViewBody(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Places the view on the body: HumanView_UpdateBody (igi2 0x4D6510), for the view alone.

remarks.para: The view looks along the body's pitch plus its own and the body's heading plus its own sideways turn. A shaking view takes three draws from the run stream for a random pitch, roll and turn, each up to the shake's angle times what is left of the shake.

The eyes are above the feet by the posture's height (HumanView_GetOriginalViewPosition, igi2 0x4D7150): 6922.24 standing, 4096 crouched, 1228.8 lying. A lean moves them along the view's own axes; a shake moves them sideways and up by two more draws, up to its range, and then runs down by its time. A landing dips them by its offset times the sine of an angle that swings on a fifteenth of a half turn each tick until the dip is over. When the eyes are moved, a line from where they would be to where they are put stops them 204.8 short of whatever it meets.

With the first-person model registered, a line 2048 ahead along the view finds how far the held object is to be pulled back from what is in front of it, and the pull steps toward that: 113.8 a tick while something is there, 75.9 a tick back out once nothing is. The model stands at the eyes plus that pull along the view and its share of a landing's dip, turned from the view by the object's own pitch and turn; and, asked to, its clip steps by its step.

member.param: Whether the first-person clip steps, isUpdateAnim: the tick's update does, placing the view alone does not.

member.summary: A trigger defined for the anim-sound type, AnimSound_TriggerAnimTriggerHandler: the reload's clicks and the like, baked into the clips. AnimTrigger_Trigger sends a trigger to its type's handler, not to the object the clip plays on, so whichever human's clip fires one, the sound plays.

member.summary: Finds the ground under a move and settles the feet on it: Human_GroundCollision (igi2 0x4FD130).
member.param: Where it ends; its height is moved onto the ground when the human lands there.
How far below the feet the ground still counts as underfoot.

remarks.para: Two vertical lines go out together: one down ten metres from above the destination, and one up two metres from it for the roof. A roof is a hit facing down; one lower than 1.8 metres raises the low-roof signal. With nothing below, the first line is cast up ten metres instead, and only a surface facing up counts.

The struck object alone is then probed again, from 1638.4 above the hit down through it, on its finest collision level. That probe's material replaces the footing's, and its light is averaged into the human's. A living human with a brain on a graph casts nothing and stands on the graph instead (). The human stands when the drop to the ground is within the tolerance, or within two metres while a slope slides it. Standing puts the feet on the ground, turns the ground's normals up, keeps hold of what is underfoot, and measures the slope of the step.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.Move
member.summary: One move of the body: Human_Move (igi2 0x5015F0).

remarks.para: The platform underfoot carries the start first. The speed is then the body's own, plus whatever a conveyor pushes. On ground the animation's step is slowed by the slope (the sine of the normal's height as a quarter turn), and a slope steeper than about fifty degrees sets an ideal slide that the sliding speed eases a tenth of the way toward each tick. The step, the slide and a decaying impact are added, and what the body carries into the air is that sum plus the platform's own speed.

The target is checked against the walls, then the ground, then other humans. The body then stands there; its acceleration and its speed through the world are measured, and its place on the platform is noted again. The sum's first axis stays on the FPU through every addition, while the other two are stored at each step, as the original does.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.UpdatePlatformMovement(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d@,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Carries the body with the rigid object it stands on: Human_UpdatePlatformMovement (igi2 0x502780).
member.param: The position to carry, which the platform's turn and travel since the body was placed on it move.
Whether to carry the position, and measure the platform's speed.
Whether to turn the body with the platform.
member.remarks: A body that was just popped out skips one step. The body's turn is read back from the platform's orientation times the body's orientation relative to it, through Real32x9_GetAngles; the position is the platform's plus the relative position turned by the inverse of the platform's orientation when the body was placed, times its orientation now. On a platform that does not move that gives back the same place, as nearly as the arithmetic allows; the original recomputes it every tick all the same.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.UpdatePlatformPosition(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)

member.param: Note the position even if the platform did not ask.
Note the orientation even if the platform did not ask.
member.remarks: Taken when the body first stands on a platform, and after every move the animation stepped. The relative position is the body's less the platform's, with the platform's orientation now kept transposed; the relative orientation is that transpose times the body's.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human.UpdateBody
member.summary: Turns the body by the turn input and rebuilds its orientation: Human_UpdateBody (igi2 0x500F30).

remarks.para: The horizontal look input times π times the view's field of view is this tick's turn; a locked body does not turn. A body that turns on a rigid platform first takes the platform's turn () and notes its new orientation on the platform afterwards. The turn is added to the ideal heading, which is not wrapped, and becomes the heading and the turning speed.

The orientation is Real32x9_Create of the angles. A body lying flat, or dead, is then tilted onto the ground under it: the averaged ground normal is taken into the body's frame, two fpatans give the pitch and the roll that stand it on that normal, and the orientation is multiplied by the tilt they make.

A lying body's turn is first checked for room () and refused whole when it has none. A body riding something () reads no turn input: its angles are those of what it rides times its own orientation there.

member.summary: The orientation from the angles, tilted onto the ground when lying or dead (Human_UpdateBody's end).

member.summary: Keeps a move out of the walls: Human_ObjectCollision (igi2 0x4FBA60).
member.param: Where it would end; moved out of the walls, and kept from rising under a ceiling.
Receives the move as it now is.

remarks.para: The sweep casts a ring of eight lines, a tenth of a metre out and lengthened by the move, at three heights for the posture. When the body moves it adds a tenth of a metre along the move at each height, and it casts one line straight up for the ceiling. Every line is in a frame turned with the body about the vertical only.

The ceiling is read first. It takes postures away (a crouch can't stand under 1.8 metres) and keeps the body from rising, and a ceiling close above makes the move slide along it and along the ground. Then every wall line that struck, from the highest down, pushes the body back out of any wall nearer than the ring, and slides the move along the wall: first along the wall's horizontal direction, then along its whole normal. Walls above the ceiling are ignored.

The horizontal slides are remembered. Two walls that are not one wall and do not face each other are a corner, and two that face each other closer than half a metre are a gap: either stops the move dead, which is why a body cannot squeeze into a corner. The pushes are averaged, and the move's height is never changed except by the ceiling.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2HumanAnimation
member.summary: A human's main animation: the clip its state plays, through the weapon it holds, HumanAnim_t.

remarks.para: A body has two main controllers and plays on one of them. Setting a clip (HumanAnim_SetAnimation, igi2 0x58F110) puts it on the other controller, blends across over the blend time in ticks (4800 a second, truncated), and makes that one the active controller; the one handed over from stops triggering its events.

A state picks its clip through its row of the state-animation table and the held weapon's clips for the body's rig (HumanAnim_SetAnimationAndTimeFromState, 0x58FAA0). The two weapon-raise rows that lower the weapon start from the clip's end less the time asked for and step backwards a frame a tick. A body holding no weapon plays its rig's stand clip whatever the state.

The upper body has its own pair of controllers (HumanAnim_Init, 0x58F650), set the same way (HumanAnim_SetUpperBodyAnimationFromHeader, 0x58F300) or cleared to leave the main clip on the whole body (HumanAnim_ClearUpperBodyAnimation, 0x58F5E0). An upper-body clip that is the main clip too does not trigger its events twice. A controller that steps itself does so in : the main one handed over from, while it blends out, and both upper-body ones always.

The controllers sit under three blenders as HumanAnim_Init wires them: the main blend between the two main controllers, the upper body's swap between its two, and over both the mix of the upper body into the main clip, the one the body's pose is taken from (). The main controllers animate every bone; the upper body's, and its swap, the lower body branch, which in these rigs holds the spine, arms and head; the main blend and the mix the center branch. Both main and swap blends take a finished blend's old clip away.
The clip's root translation does not move the body — only the states' own movement and do; it places the root bone.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2HumanChannels
member.summary: A human's channel block: this tick's 63 control values and last tick's.

remarks.para: Human_s.avChannel and avLastChannel. Whatever drives the human — the player's input task or an AI — hands it a full frame once a tick through the HumanUpdate event, and the handler (HumanPlayer_HumanUpdateHandler, igi2 0x4B9A80) copies the current frame to the last one before taking the new one, unless the channels are locked. Every "pressed this tick" test the state machines make is that pair: non-zero now and zero last tick.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2HumanView.UpdateView(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2HumanChannels,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Aims the view up or down from the look input: HumanView_UpdateView (igi2 0x4D62F0).
member.param: The human's channels: the vertical look, and the field-of-view buttons.
Whether Smooth Motion bypasses tick averaging and the fine-aim curve.

remarks.para: At the default field of view the vertical look is the average of this tick's and last tick's input; zoomed in, it is this tick's alone. The step is π times the input times the field of view, so a narrow view aims finely. Input below 0.06 is eased further, divided by two less its size times 16⅔, which takes the jitter out of small mouse movements. The aim is held within 85 degrees up and down.

The pitch looked at is the aim plus the kick and the breathing; the sideways turn is its aim plus its kick, held within a quarter turn. The field-of-view buttons narrow it by four percent, widen it by the same step, or put it back.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2ContentModules
member.summary: I.G.I. 2: Covert Strike's content, as the modules a session registers.
member.remarks: The list grows one module per gameplay milestone. Everything not covered by a module still loads: a type level data declares with no class behind it becomes a DeclaredTask placeholder with its parameters intact, so a level is always structurally complete and only ever behaviourally partial.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2ContentModules.All
member.summary: Gets every module, in the order a session registers them.
member.remarks: Order is behaviour: a module whose natives another module's tables call has to declare first, and the original's own start-up order is the specification for it.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2ScriptVocabularyModule
member.summary: The script identifiers every I.G.I. 2 level depends on.

remarks.para: There are only five, and they were counted rather than discovered. Reading the symbol tables of all 24 shipped objects.qvm together gives the complete vocabulary a level rests on: the two task commands and TRUE/FALSE, which the engine already provides, plus these. Finding them one failing level at a time would have taken as many passes as there are levels and still left no evidence the list was complete.

The values come from igi2.exe — AISquad_RegisterScriptValues (0x49A880) for the AI types and OverlayHolder_Open (0x533BC0) for the overlays. Reading them mattered more than it looks: a wrong value does not fail. It lands as a parameter on a task, the tree still builds, and it resurfaces much later looking like a gameplay bug with no trace back to here.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2ScriptVocabularyModule.LoadTables(OpenIGI.Engine.Titles.ContentLoadContext)
member.remarks: At start-up, Config_LoadConfig: the player profiles out of config.qvm.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2PlayerContentModule
member.summary: The player the level places.

remarks.para: The player is the first game's with the sequel's six further parameters bound (): its starting weapons, first-person model, visibility triple and carry-over flag. What the class carries that a placeholder cannot is the level's own spawn: PlayerSpawn looks for a HumanPlayerTask, and without one a level that declares its player perfectly well appears to declare none.

That absence was not a missing feature but a failing mission. Dropped where the debugging camera opens rather than where the level puts him, the player stands outside the AreaActivate volume the mission is played inside; location1/level1's LevelFlow reads !AreaActivate_178.nActive as "left the area", sends its LEFT_AREA message, and fails the mission about two and a half seconds in -- the grace period MainMenu state 9 counts out.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2PlayerContentModule.LoadTables(OpenIGI.Engine.Titles.ContentLoadContext)
member.remarks: The player's tuning, out of humanplayer.qvm, as Flow_CreateHandler (igi2 0x401600) reads it before any level. A character's model and animations arrive with the level's packs.

member.remarks: Ahead of the player's module, because Flow_CreateHandler (igi2 0x401600) loads the weapons before the player's tuning and the tuning names them by their WEAPON_ID_* and AMMO_ID_* constants.

member.remarks: SoundSys_Open (igi2 0x42E9A0) registers them at start-up; nothing is read until a level is, when Game_CreateHandler (0x4070E0) runs the game's, the location's and the mission's scripts.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2TerrainContentModule
member.summary: The terrain's task types: the tile grid, its placement, its material table and its holes.

remarks.para: Without these the four types load as placeholders — the tree is right and the parameter values are there, but nothing knows a tile has an id, so no .thm, .tmm or .tlm is ever asked for and the level renders with no ground.

fails the other way round: unregistered it loads as a placeholder and the ground it should have taken away is drawn, so the hillside runs straight through the vehicle ramp cut into it. Four of the shipped levels need it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2TerrainContentModule.LoadTables(OpenIGI.Engine.Titles.ContentLoadContext)
member.remarks: Nothing to load. A terrain's tables are its own child tasks and its tiles' map files, both of which arrive with the level rather than before it.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2ForestContentModule
member.summary: The forest's task types: a stand of trees and the wind that moves it.
member.remarks: Without these the two types load as placeholders, so nothing knows a stand has a level id, and without the id nothing can name its forest_%d.dat — the placement file is named by the task rather than by a parameter, so an unrecognised task means an unreachable file.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2DataLayout
member.summary: Where retail I.G.I. 2 keeps its data.

remarks.para: Read off a retail 1.1 installation and off igi2.exe's own strings, which carry the alias targets verbatim — LOCAL:common/textures/%s, LOCAL:common/fonts/font1.fnt, MISSION:sounds/, LANGUAGE:objectives.res, COMPUTER:computer.res. The alias vocabulary is identical to I.G.I. 1's; only the targets differ, and most of those do not.

The data root is the installation's pc directory, so these paths are relative to that and read exactly like I.G.I. 1's. The directories are upper case on disk (MISSIONS, COMMON), which is invisible on Windows and will need case-insensitive resolution on Linux; that belongs to the virtual file system rather than here.
TODO(phase-1): moves to OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2DataLayout.MissionScriptName
member.remarks: Unchanged from I.G.I. 1: every level directory holds a mission.qvm.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2DataLayout.SharedArchives
member.remarks: I.G.I. 2 packs a level's own textures and models beside it rather than in one shared archive per kind, so there is no equivalent of I.G.I. 1's common/sprites/sprites.res pair to mount for every mission. Left empty until a level actually needs one, rather than guessing at a name.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2DataLayout.StringArchives(System.String)
member.remarks: The two the game's own text is read from, the status messages' and the computer's (). Its tree ships LANGUAGE/ in upper case beside MISSIONS; the local device finds either casing.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2DataLayout.StructuralTaskTypes
member.remarks: I.G.I. 1's set less Container, which I.G.I. 2's editor declares with a parameter of its own. Pre-registering the engine's parameterless one fails the arity check on every I.G.I. 2 level; the other five are undeclared by both games.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2Runtime
member.summary: I.G.I. 2: Covert Strike, as far as the engine can currently run it.
member.remarks: The layout and the format profile are measured against a retail installation. The module list covers what the gameplay milestones have reached and no more; every type it does not cover still loads, as a DeclaredTask placeholder carrying its declared parameters, so all 24 shipped levels build correct trees at every stage and gain behaviour a module at a time.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2AlarmControlTask
member.summary: A level's alarm, I.G.I. 2's AlarmControl: a Terminal (itself an ExplodeObject) whose scripts say when its alarm is triggered and when it sounds, exporting isTrigger, isAlarm and nTriggerLastTick beside the terminal's isInUse, isLastInUse, isActive, isHacked, isHackedThisTick, nClientID and nTeam, and the explodable's isExploded.

remarks.para: The terminal's tick (Terminal_RunHandler, igi2 0x4CA9E0): a hack finished last tick is made, and stands for one tick as hacked this tick; it ticks as an ExplodeObject; exploded, it is no longer active, and otherwise its Active script, where it has one, says whether it is; in use is kept while it was hacked at in the last two ticks.

Then the alarm's (AlarmControl_RunHandler, 0x4D0320): last tick's alarm is kept; exploded or inactive, it is neither triggered nor sounding; otherwise its trigger script says whether it is triggered, which stamps the level's tick, and its alarm script whether it sounds. An alarm that starts raises AIEVENT_ALARMON and counts once on the player's nTimesAlarmTriggered; one that stops raises AIEVENT_ALARMOFF. Both go to every team, from nowhere and no one.

A human hacks it as a timed action at its model's second vertex, kneeling 0.675 m out, for its hack time. The multiplayer team a hack hands it over to (Change Team When Hacked?, Start Team, Link To Terminal) is not in the sequel's single-player levels and not ported.

member.content: Its save state, AlarmControl_ptSerializeParameterList: a terminal's, then whether it is triggered, sounds and sounded, and when it was last triggered.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2CabinetTask
member.summary: A cabinet, I.G.I. 2's Cabinet (cabinet.c): an object turned by its heading that the player searches as a timed action from its model's first magic vertex, while its drawer, the attach point of the magic type Drawer, slides out and back on the search clip's triggers. The level's scripts follow it through isInUse, isLastInUse and isSearched.

remarks.para: Cabinet_RunHandler: its children run; a drawer on the move runs; it stays in use while it was searched at in the last two ticks. Drawer_RunHandler: opening, the drawer is out by its full 0.2 m at once; closing, it is in at once; told to snap, it snaps; either way it then stands still.
Cabinet_EvaluateActivateHandler: from its first magic vertex, to a view in front of it within three quarters of a metre to either side. Cabinet_ActivateHandler: in use, as of this tick.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2ConveyorBeltTask
member.summary: A conveyor belt, I.G.I. 2's ConveyorBelt: a placed object whose faces of the ConveyorBelt material carry what stands on them along its own X and Y.

remarks.para: A human standing on it asks it each move what pushes it (ConveyorBelt_PushObjectHandler, igi2 0x53A7D0): where its footing's material is the belt's, the push is the belt's speeds, metres a second made units a tick, turned by the belt's frame; anywhere else on it nothing. Its speeds are set by level data and by ConveyorBelt_SetSpeed (0x53A5F0), each held within twenty metres a second either way.
It runs as any placed object does, its children only (ConveyorBelt_RunHandler, 0x53A790), and is still placed by the world scene, which reads its parameters by name ().

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2DoorTask
member.summary: A door or gate that swings or slides between shut and open, I.G.I. 2's Door, exporting isLocked, isOpen, isClosed, isLastClosed, isLastOpen, isPicked and nDoorOpenTicks.

remarks.para: Its state is one number, how far open it is (vRealPos, 0 to 1), which moves toward where it is told to be by one thirtieth of its Open time a tick (Door_RunHandler, igi2 0x5377B0). Shut, its open script may tell it to open; open, its close script may tell it to close; and its locked script says, each tick, whether it is locked. Where it stands follows from that number (Door_SetPosition, 0x5362B0): slid along its stop offsets from its start, and turned about its Z by that fraction of its Max angle.

A human's view finds it (Door_EvaluateActivateHandler, 0x537600) from either side while it is unlocked or can be picked; activated, it opens or closes (Door_ToggleOpenDoorEx, 0x5384D0). A door that stops on collision holds where it is for fifteen ticks when a human's lines strike it from the side it is moving toward (Door_TraceLinesHandler, 0x536FE0).
It is still placed by the world scene, which reads its parameters by name ().

member.summary: A door's link to the sector portal it stands in.

member.summary: Finds the portal it stands in, Door_AttachToPortal: a line along its own Y through its model's middle, half a metre each way, traced for portal faces one way and then the other.
member.param: The collision world, whose stationary objects the lines are traced against.

remarks.para: Any portal it held before is let go open. A door that does not link up, has no model, or is see-through links to nothing. Both lines must strike a sector's portal below sixty-four; then each portal's byte is written open unless the door is shut, and the place it is drawn when shut and seen from the portal's side is its model's middle moved by its of the way to the middle of the two portal hits.
See-through is RigidDynCubeObj_IsTransparent, which asks the render mesh's records for a blend flag; the port asks the model's draw records whether any is a transparent face group.

remarks.para: Its tick (EditRigidObj_RunHandler, igi2 0x5B4860) runs its attached object's, which is no task here, then its children's. What else it does is drawing: its draw queue, shadow protection for one noted as a wall, and portal clipping.

A guide turns and moves it; its solids go with it, and its children attached to it follow. A level's queue below the normal one is raised to it when read (EditRigidObj_UpdateInternalDataHandler, 0x5B4950); the world scene draws the queue as authored.

member.summary: A timed action, I.G.I. 2's GenericTBA: an ExplodeObject the player works at, exporting isInUse, isLastInUse, isActive, isFinished, isFinishedThisTick and nClientID beside isExploded.

remarks.para: Its tick (GenericTBA_RunHandler, igi2 0x4C2200): a finish set last tick is made, and stands for one tick as finished this tick. One that is explodable then ticks as an ExplodeObject does, its script saying when it blows; one that is not, once finished, wears its destroyed model and runs its children, once. Exploded, it is no longer active; otherwise its script, where it has one, says whether it is. In use is kept while it was used in the last two ticks.
It answers bullets and blasts as any ExplodeObject does; one that is not explodable only counts them.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2FenceTask
member.summary: A fence, I.G.I. 2's Fence (fence.c): a rigid object turned by its heading alone, which the player climbs over while it is dead, and which shocks the human against it and hums while its electric expression holds. Its model's first two magic vertices mark its ends along its X.

remarks.para: Fence_RunHandler: its electric expression, chopped to a byte, or nought with none, says whether it is live; a fence that comes alive makes an ambient area of elfence_loop two metres up over its middle, as long as it is with a metre and a half to spare, 1.75 m deep and two high, fading over ten metres; one that dies deletes it; then its children run.

Fence_NotifyHandler: live, it shocks a human whose raised feet are within 0.6 m of its ends along it, 0.6 m of it across, and between a metre below it and three above. Fence_EvaluateActivateHandler: dead and climbable, it is taken outright by a view across it within reach and between its ends, facing it within a sixth of a turn.
