member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2HostInteraction
member.summary: Another game's door or switch, as I.G.I. 2's player finds and uses what it may activate (): the engine's own interaction (), which that game's player uses alike.

remarks.para: A switch is pressed, a door that is not locked opens or shuts, and the task each stands for is told it was used, which that game's alarms and scripts read, as its own player using it tells them. A locked door that game lets its player pick is picked as I.G.I. 2's player picks its own, for as long as that game's picking takes, and is then that game's picked lock: open, and open to that game's scripts for good.

A terminal, a timed action and a spot to plant a charge are worked as I.G.I. 2's player works its own terminal and timed actions: held for as long as that game's work takes, each tick of it that game's use, and its end that game's finish. A charge so planted stands where it was worked from. A cabinet is searched as I.G.I. 2's are, for as long as that game's search takes, and is then that game's searched cabinet; its drawer is that game's to show.

A fence is climbed over as I.G.I. 2's are, across that game's fence, while it is not electrified. A wire is strung between that game's two ends, as I.G.I. 2 strings its own, and is held, climbed along or slid down as that game's slope says; in use while it is held.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2LadderTask
member.summary: A ladder, I.G.I. 2's Ladder (ladder.c): a rigid object the player climbs. Its model's magic vertices mark it: the first its top for finding it from above, the second its foot and the third its top for climbing, the zeroth its foot for sliding down.

remarks.para: Ladder_UpdateSteps: its steps are the height between its second and third vertices over 1228.8 units, chopped.

Ladder_EvaluateActivateHandler, from its foot: a view less than one and a half metres ahead of it along its Y (or less than three quarters behind it) and within 0.7 m to either side, facing it within a quarter turn, between its foot and its first vertex in height, takes it outright when a line from the view to it at the view's height is clear. Then, from its top: a view on the climbing side of its first vertex that resolves it, with a clear line to that vertex, takes it from the top. A blocked line forgets the best target found so far.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2LiftTask
member.summary: A lift that carries what stands on it from floor to floor, I.G.I. 2's Lift, exporting nInactive, nCurrentFloor, isMoving, isStart and isStop.

remarks.para: Its floors are its children, in order. Standing still, its Floor up script sends it to the next floor and its Floor down script to the one before (Lift_RunHandler, igi2 0x46E420); while its Can start script allows, it moves along the way between them (Lift_Move, 0x46DBA0): its speed eases toward its top speed by its inertia each tick, and in the last tenth of the way slows with what is left of it.

Where it stands follows from how far along it is (Lift_UpdatePosition, 0x46D640): the position straight between the floors, the orientation slerped between theirs. What it holds moves with it (), and a body standing on it rides it as on any moving platform.
It is still placed by the world scene, which reads its parameters by name ().

member.content: Its save state, Lift_ptSerializeParameterList: a model object's, then the floor it heads for, where its way starts and stops and where it stood, its frames as authored, at either end and as it stood, its speed and how far along it is, the ticks it has stood, its five flags and its floors.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2MineFieldTask
member.summary: A minefield, I.G.I. 2's MineField (minefield.c): when its Explode expression holds, a blast goes off at the task it is told to explode close to, and again after its delay between explosions.

remarks.para: MineField_RunHandler: the pause left counts down; at nought, the expression is run, and if it holds the field explodes and the pause is set to the delay between explosions in ticks. A delay of -1 makes the pause -30, which never comes back to nought: it explodes once. A pause of exactly -1 stops it.

MineField_Explode: nothing goes off at a dead human; elsewhere the target's camera-target position, snapped to the ground under or over it when asked, takes an explosion (Explosion0_New): once, after its delay, with its damage scale over its radius and falloff, a burn of 1.5 metres, its fragments (1009_01_1) and fireballs and sound, no AI event, the minefield as its owner, falling off in a straight line.

member.content: Its save state, MineField_ptSerializeParameterList: the ticks before it may explode again.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2SwitchTask
member.content: Its save state, Switch_ptSerializeParameterList: whether it is on and was, is and was destroyed, is and was pressed, when it was last pressed, and whether it can be.
member.summary: A switch or button the player presses, I.G.I. 2's Switch, exporting isActive, isOn, isLastOn, isPressed, isLastPressed, isDestroyed, isLastDestroyed and nClientID.

remarks.para: A press (Switch_Pressed, igi2 0x4DB3E0) holds it pressed and notes the level's tick. Switch_RunHandler (0x4DA760): its children run, its Active script says whether it can be found; three ticks after the press it lets go; the tick it is first held it flips on or off and sounds at itself; and it wears the model its state names (Switch_SetModel, 0x4DA360): on, on and pressed, off, off and pressed, destroyed.

A human's view finds it (Switch_EvaluateActivateHandler, 0x4DACE0) while it is whole and active, from in front of it — along its Y axis — and within 3072 units of its centre line across, measured from its model's first magic vertex.

A round that strikes it (Switch_WeaponHitHandler, Project I.G.I.'s 0x445840 the same) destroys it when it is Destructable, whichever game's round it is: the handler reads nothing of the hit. Nothing finds it after that, but its run copies isDestroyed to isLastDestroyed before it sets its model, so it wears the destroyed one only once its on or pressed state next changes. Project I.G.I.'s run (0x4450F0) copies after, and swaps at once.
It is still placed by the world scene, which reads its parameters by name ().

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Interaction.Igi2SecurityCameraTask
member.content: Its save state, SCamera_ptSerializeParameterList: a model object's, then whether it saw a dead friend, is on, sees and saw, how long it has seen, and whether it is destroyed. Its lens is its SCameraLens child in retail, a part here.
member.summary: A security camera, I.G.I. 2's SCamera with its SCameraLens: a lens on a holder that sweeps, looks for the other side and for its own side's dead, follows what it sees and, after a moment, detects it; exporting isDetection, isLastDetection, nDetectionTime and isExploded.

remarks.para: Its tick (SCamera_RunHandler, igi2 0x48F9E0): its lens first, then, destroyed, it is off and tells the AI every thirty ticks; otherwise its script, where it has one, says whether it is on.

The lens's tick (SCamera_SCameraLensRunHandler, 0x48EF20): on, it tilts back to its authored tilt, looks (, on side one, for live enemies and dead friends among humans and cameras), turns (SCamera_RotateLens, 0x48E7A0) and beeps; off, it tilts down and detects nothing. Hit hard enough, it explodes and the camera is destroyed.

Turning, it takes the first dead friend in plain sight, then the first enemy in plain sight over it; a new target restarts the detection clock (two, one or three quarters of three seconds by difficulty), and detection comes when it runs out. It follows a target outside five degrees of its aim at three quarters of a degree a tick, within its limits; with none, after two seconds it sweeps between its limits at its speed, holding at each end for its delay.
The visible lens follows the collision frame; its indicator uses the lens model's first magic vertex.

member.content: Its save state, Wire_ptSerializeParameterList: a model object's, then whether it is cut at and was.
member.summary: A wire strung between two points, I.G.I. 2's Wire (wire.c): climbed hand over hand while it is near level, ridden down while it slopes, its model stretched between its ends and its first two magic vertices its ends. The level's scripts follow it through isInUse and isLastInUse.

remarks.para: Wire_UpdateInternalDataHandler: at its ends' midpoint, its Y pointed down the span and scaled by its length over a metre (). Wire_GetOrientation: the frame along its magic vertices, which is its own. Wire_IsSliding: its tilt, taken as an angle of nought to a full turn, more than two degrees.

Wire_EvaluateActivateHandler: the point on it nearest the view between its ends is offered, while its useable expression, where it has one, holds. Wire_ActivateHandler: in use. Wire_RunHandler: what was in use is last in use; its children do not run.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Menus.Igi2InGameMenu
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's in-game menu, the MenuManager GameScreen_CreateHandler makes of LOCAL:menusystem/ingamemenu.qsc (gamescreen.c, menumanager.c): its screens, the stack it pushes them on, its popup, and the status it runs through, with every native its script calls.

remarks.para: The OpenIGI shell presents the menu, so drawing, layout and keyboard handling are not kept: a screen's fade takes the eight ticks it would take to draw, and the shell calls , and the windows' own methods where the retail menu would read the keyboard.

MenuManager_RunHandler: opening a screen takes its data in (MenuWindow_eInitDataEvent) unless it is opened without; a fade in leads to input, a fade out to the status asked for; idle, a failed level whose player still lives opens the menu by itself after five seconds, pausing the game; the quit, main menu and restart statuses ask the game for them.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Paths.Igi2SplinePathGuideTask
member.summary: What moves an object along a spline path, I.G.I. 2's SplinePathGuideQTask, exporting vPosition (segment and the share of it run) and vSpeed (the speed's scale).

remarks.para: Its tick (SplinePathGuideQTask_RunHandler, igi2 0x5E67F0): its speed is taken as the tick's scale, and its children run with it as the guide SplinePathGuide_SetRunning starts and stops. Running, on a path of three nodes or more and with a model to move, it steps the share of its segment by the unit length's share there times the speed between the segment's nodes, in world units a tick, times the scale. Past the end of a segment it carries what is over into the next by the ratio of their lengths; past the last, it starts again from the first when looping, else it stops at the end. The model is turned and moved to where the curve then is, and the step it took is the guide's velocity.

Reading one (SplinePathGuideQTask_UpdateInternalDataHandler, 0x5E6650) holds its start position to between nought and one, puts it at that share of its path's whole length when it is past nought, sets it running if it runs from the start, and takes its speed from its scale. It connects to its model once the level is loaded (SplinePathGuideQTask_UpdateInternalDataAfterLoadHandler, 0x5E6700).

member.content: Its save state, SplinePathGuideQTask_ptSerializeParameterList: the path it follows, the object it moves, the segment it is on, its flags and how far along the segment it is.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Paths.Igi2SplinePathNodeTask
member.summary: One point of a spline path, I.G.I. 2's SplinePathNodeQTask: where the path passes, which way an object on it faces there, how fast it goes, and the curve's tangent.

remarks.para: Reading one (SplinePathNodeQTask_UpdateInternalDataHandler, igi2 0x547EC0) clamps its speed to no less than nought and rebuilds its whole path from the nodes read so far: so a path is built once for every node, and its frames, which each rebuild turns to their tangents, are turned again each time.
Its Tangent is used as authored only when UseComputedTangent is off; otherwise the path works it out from its neighbours.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Paths.Igi2SplinePathNodeTask.LimitOrientation
member.summary: Turns the frame to the tangent, SplinePathNodeQTask_LimitOrientation (igi2 0x5481E0), and takes its quaternion as SplinePathDynCubeObj_UpdateOrientations (0x5491A0) does.

remarks.para: With no tangent the frame is the identity. A free-oriented node keeps its frame. Otherwise its Y becomes the tangent, its X the tangent across the old Z, and its Z that X across the tangent, each made a unit; a tangent along the old Z takes its Z across the world's X instead, from the tangent stored to floats.
The tangent's doubles go into the products whole: only the results are chopped.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Paths.Igi2SplinePathTask
member.summary: A spline path an object is guided along, I.G.I. 2's SplinePathDynCubeObj: its child nodes joined by cubic Hermite segments.

remarks.para: A path of fewer than three nodes is never measured nor ridden. Its nodes are its SplinePathNodeQTask children, the first hundred, in order (SplinePathDynCubeObj_ResetPath, igi2 0x5486F0).

Measuring it (SplinePathDynCubeObj_InitPath, 0x548DA0): a node that computes its tangent takes the step to the next for the first, from the one before for the last, and half the step across its neighbours between. Each segment's length is summed over a hundred steps of a hundredth, and each tenth of it over twenty steps of a two-hundredth; and each node's time from the start is the last one's plus the segment's length over the mean of the two speeds.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Paths.Igi2SplinePathTask.Position(System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Where a segment passes, SplinePathDynCubeObj_GetInterpolatedPosition (igi2 0x5487B0): the cubic Hermite of its two nodes' positions and tangents.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject
member.summary: A rigid object physics moves, PhysicsObj_s: a body, its contact points and the tick that moves it through the world (PhysicsObj_Update, igi2 0x5AF350), with the client's 24-bit truncating FPU arithmetic in disassembly order.

remarks.para: A tick: gravity and the air and spin damping (); then, with collision detection on, each contact point is traced along its velocity and the first that strikes and is not leaving the surface bounces the body and rubs it (). Fast enough, the object moves by its velocity; any point that ends up inside a surface lifts it out and loses the speed into that surface ().
Positions are doubles, but every addition to one goes through the FPU at 24 bits, so a moved position keeps only a float's precision, as the client's does.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject.Update(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsWorld)
member.summary: Moves the object a tick, PhysicsObj_Update (igi2 0x5AF350).
member.param: The gravity, units a tick squared.
What the velocity keeps each tick.
What the angular momentum keeps each tick, and each contact.
member.remarks: The orientation and position are taken first. Then the forces, and the contacts if detection is on; an object held level loses its vertical speed. Only faster than does the position take the velocity; held level, the orientation is rebuilt about its old third row. Any point inside a surface then lifts the object out, the object takes its new position, and the change from the last is kept. Attachments and the change of orientation, which only what rides on an object reads, are not kept.

member.summary: Gravity and the damping, PhysicsObj_AddNonContactForces (igi2 0x5AF1C0): the type's weight, turned into the body's frame, acts at the centre; the body takes its step, and its spin and velocity are damped.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject.AddContactForces(System.Single,System.Single,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsWorld)
member.summary: The contacts, PhysicsObj_AddContactForces (igi2 0x5AEC90): each point is traced from where it is along its velocity, and the first one to strike something it is not leaving bounces the body and rubs it.
member.returns: Zero for no contact, one for a contact, two for one meeting the surface faster than a unit a tick.

remarks.para: A hit counts when its distance is within the point's speed plus , or whenever the material it leaves has density; an owner that lets physics objects through (glass, water) does not count, and slows the next contact's body to a quarter.

The first counting hit whose point is not separating faster than a unit a tick is the contact: the surface's normal is kept on the point, the point is marked in contact, and the collision and friction responses follow. The trace stops there.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject.CollisionResponse(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The bounce, PhysicsObj_CollisionResponse (igi2 0x5AFC20): the impulse along the normal that turns the point's approach into the bounce's share of it, applied to the spin and the centre; then whatever velocity is left into the surface is taken away.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject.FrictionResponse(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The rub, PhysicsObj_FrictionResponse (igi2 0x5B00D0): against the direction of travel along the surface, the friction of the weight on it, never more than the velocity that way; and the spin is damped.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject.AssertNoIntersection(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsWorld,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d@)
member.summary: Lifts the object out of the ground, PhysicsObj_AssertNoIntersection (igi2 0x5ADCA0): from 2048 units above each contact point straight down to it, the deepest surface struck above the point raises the new position by its depth, and each struck surface takes away the velocity going into it.
member.remarks: The test starts from where the object is, not where it is going. The velocity it changes is not re-approximated, and the height is added at 24 bits whether or not it is raised.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2RigidBody
member.summary: A rigid body's mass, inertia and motion, Physics_s, and the integrator that moves it a tick (Physics_Update, igi2 0x5A9580), with the client's 24-bit truncating FPU arithmetic in disassembly order.

remarks.para: Forces are gathered in the body's frame and summed once a tick: their sum, over the mass, turned into the world by the orientation, is the change of velocity; the moments they make about the centre are added to the angular momentum, which is kept in the body's frame. The angular velocity is the momentum through the inverse inertia, turned into the world. The orientation is stepped as a quaternion and written back as a matrix.
An orientation is nine floats row by row; a body vector goes into the world as each row's dot with it.
The steps Project I.G.I.'s build compiled alike are the engine's shared ones (); the angular velocity, the quaternion step and the length estimate are this build's own.

member.summary: Moves the body a tick, Physics_Update (igi2 0x5A9580).
member.param: The orientation, nine floats row by row; turned by the body's spin.
member.returns: Whether the body turned: when it had no angular momentum.

remarks.para: The orientation becomes a quaternion first. The queued forces are summed, and each one acting off the centre adds its moment; the sum over the mass, turned into the world, is added to the velocity, the moments to the angular momentum, and the queue is emptied.

With angular momentum, the angular velocity is it through the inverse inertia, turned into the world. The quaternion takes a step of half the angular velocity times itself, is normalised twice and is written back as the orientation.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Pickups.Igi2GunPickup
member.summary: A weapon lying in the level, GunPickup: where it lies, the weapon and rounds it gives, and the test a human passes to take it.

remarks.para: A RigidDynCubeObj carrying the weapon's Fixed Model. GunPickup_UpdateInternalDataHandler (igi2 0x46BA00) works out what it gives: a grenade or a medipack one round in its load and one for its first fire type, anything else a full load and nothing more for the first; the second fire type always a full load of its own.

Each tick GunPickup_RunHandler (0x46A760) lets a pickup still falling fall, and deletes one that was taken. A pickup the level places starts at rest, so for it the handler is only the deleting. A thrown one (, GunPickup_New, 0x46C2F0) falls (). Not yet: a multiplayer game's respawn.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Pickups.Igi2GunPickup.Fall(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Collision.IIgi2CollisionQuery,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.IgiRandom,System.Action{System.String,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d})
member.summary: A falling pickup's tick, GunPickup_RunHandler (igi2 0x46A9B5): gravity, then six lines from where it is, four to points around it on the plane of the ground it last fell on and two straight down and up; what the four strike pushes and slows it, what lies below lands it, and its speed carries it on.
member.param: The run stream the drop sound draws from.
Plays a sound at a point.

remarks.para: The four points lie a radius ahead and behind along Y and 819.2 above and below, each with its own component along the ground normal taken off, then moved by the speed. A surface other than the ground among them turns the speed away from its face, loses a hundred and twentieth of it, and adds where the line struck short of its point to a correction, averaged over them.

Below: the ground's normal is kept, and within two metres the fall slows to 409.6 a tick at most. Within 819.2 the pickup lands: the drop sound plays the first time (one of two, by a draw); on a slope steeper than about 37 degrees it slides, otherwise it stops there, ceases falling if it is the ground, and is turned to lie along it. Its height ends 122.88 above what is below. If it fell through, the line up puts it back 2048 above what it struck. It never falls faster than 1228.8 a tick.

Water is no surface to it: the probes pass over it and, below, it lets the pickup sink (the C4 bomb alone lands on it, and if it falls under, comes back up). It comes to rest only on the ground or a building's room.

member.summary: The player's tuning, I.G.I. 2's HumanPlayerConfigItem: one task in HUMANPLAYER/humanplayer.qvm carrying the jump and air-control speeds, the peek, the damage multipliers and the two scripts that define the weapon cycle and the ammo limits.

member.summary: The status screen's action menu, actionmenuscreen.c's ActionMenuScreen: up to six things the player could do now — the object it would activate, a weapon it could take in exchange for one it carries — in an order the zoom keys rotate, of which only the first is done.

remarks.para: Each tick what is on offer registers again (); then keeps the last tick's order for what is still offered, adds what is new at the end and forgets what was not offered. The order a tick reads is the one the tick before worked out, so a thing newly offered is first only on the second tick after it was.
While an activation runs, the menu is hidden for ten ticks (), and nothing is first.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2Gameplay
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's own player for the host: the ported HumanPlayer over the level's collision.

remarks.para: The level's HumanPlayer task says where the player stands and which way it faces. The collision world is built from the same placements and ground the scene walk produced; the tuning is the one humanplayer.qvm declared at start-up. The player is made as HumanPlayer_CreateHandler makes it and ticked as the original ticks it: the channels read, HumanPlayer_Update, then the delayed half.

The body plays the clips the level's packs load, picked by state through the held weapon (), and the view carries the level's first-person model with the weapon in hand, which the host draws through . The level's sound definitions are read as the level is, and what the player and its weapons sound plays through the host's mixer. Not yet behind it: water, AI events and conveyors.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer
member.content: The action machine: the player's second state machine, beside locomotion, for what the hands do (HumanPlayer_apfAction, igi2 0x63D794).

remarks.para: Its signal is packed by HumanPlayer_ActionSignalHandler (0x4B33E0) into the same bits as the locomotion signal, with one difference: the first bit is the first-person model's clip having ended, which is what a weapon change waits on.

Ported: locked (0), idle (1), firing (2, 3, 4), reloading (5), the weapon change (6) and firing empty (9), with the upper-body modes the states set (HumanPlayer_SetUpperBody, 0x4BD2E0) and the weapon selection the update runs before the machines, peeking (7), the computer (8) and throwing (10).

member.content: What the player finds to activate, and activating it.
Jumping, falling, and the landing both end in.
The binoculars and the thermal goggles, which their own keys raise and lower over whatever is in hand.
Where the body's collision sits for each posture.
The tilt of the player's spine with its view: the bone callbacks HumanPlayer_UpdateInternalDataHandler (igi2 0x4B9850) sets on the lower back, upper back and shoulders.
member.remarks: The lower back runs first. With an upper-body clip playing it swaps its parent's turn for the clip's root key, as a soldier's does. Then it eases the view's shoulder pitch a fifth of the way toward the view's pitch (toward level unless the player stands) and tilts by a share of it; the upper back and the shoulders tilt by their own shares of that pitch. A dead player's spine is left as its clips pose it.
member.content: The player's breath: the sway a scope shows once it has been held a second, the kit rattling as the player runs, and the panting that running builds up and that dies away after.
Searching a cabinet.

The map computer: a computer key, freshly pressed on the ground, opens it on its screen; the player stands still, its view locked, while another computer key turns to that screen and the same one, a weapon key, the binoculars or the goggles, a hit or death closes it again. What the screens show is the shell's.
Making the player.
member.summary: The player, as I.G.I. 2's HumanPlayer_t runs it.

remarks.para: The player's own part over the shared body: its tuning, its signal word, its states and its action machine. It grows a retail function at a time; each member names the one it comes from. The parts of the engine the states reach into — the animation layer, the collision probe, the AI's ears, the held weapon — are behind interfaces, so the locomotion logic is testable on its own.

member.content: What the player settles once everything else has run in a tick.
The player as detectors see it.

Dropping the weapon in hand (HumanPlayer_RunActionIdle, HumanPlayer_RunActionChangeWeapon): the drop key, freshly pressed, on a weapon its type lets be dropped in a single-player game, puts it away for the next of its category, or the next there is; once the change goes ahead it lands on the ground as a pickup with its load and the ammunition carried for it, and is carried no more.
An explosion reaching the player.
Fences: the shock of a live one, telling the notified objects where the player is, and climbing over a dead one.
Firing: the action states that pull and let go the trigger, the kick the view takes, and where the player's weapon fires from (HumanPlayer_apfAction 2, 3, 4 and 9).

remarks.para: The trigger is pulled once a pull: the fire state raises on its first tick, and the update fires the weapon after the view is placed. Held fire after that is the weapon's own. The state watches the weapon: a shot that kicked is taken by the view and plays the fire mode on the upper body, a weapon gone empty puts the trigger up, and the fire key coming up lets go.
A weapon that never runs out reloads itself when empty, and the AI hears it (HumanPlayer_SendHandleWeaponAIEvent).

member.content: Flashbang exposure and fading from humanplayer.c HumanPlayer_FlashBangHandler.
Throwing a grenade, and the anim triggers its clips and the body's fire on the player.
Flinching from a hit, and dying.
Climbing ladders: getting on, the steps up and down, getting off at the top, and sliding down.
The locomotion states and the movement they share.

Peeking: while the peek key is held the player stands its ground, its body locked in its heading, and the mouse leans the view out to either side, or up out of a crouch or off the ground, as far as the player's general settings allow; the weapon is lowered aside meanwhile. Letting go returns to the stance it peeked from.
The weapons lying in the level, which the player takes as it comes within reach of them.
Lying flat and crawling.

Reloading: the action machine's reload state (HumanPlayer_apfAction 5) and its three steps, the start, the loop and the end, each on the upper body and the first-person model (upper-body modes 8, 9 and 10).
member.remarks: The rounds go in when a step's clip has played: straight after the start for a weapon with no loop, on the way into the loop or the end otherwise, and again each time round the loop; the AI hears the weapon handled at each (HumanPlayer_SendHandleWeaponAIEvent, a range of 20480).
member.content: Its save state, HumanPlayer_ptSerializeParameterList past a human's: its action machine, its weapon handling and precision, its upper body, its timed actions, its ladder, fence, wire and peek, its damage flashes, its saves used, its swimming, its grenade, its movement and its cheats.
What the level's scripts do to the player directly.
The player struck by a bullet, and the bullets it hears go by.

The silent kill: activating a soldier from behind plays the player's tba_silent_kill_jones with the soldier taken into its own silent death beside it, seen from the movement camera, until the clip ends.
How often the player has been spotted, the mission's statistic, and how it keeps low from the soldiers looking for it.
Working a mounted gun.
Swimming, states 19 to 21 (humanplayer.c HumanPlayer_InitStateSwim, HumanPlayer_RunStateSwim, HumanPlayer_RunStateTreadWater): forward, backward and treading water.
The player's tick: the order the original runs everything in.
The view's limits while lying flat.
The weapon in the player's hands as the first-person view shows it.
Wires: climbing one hand over hand, and riding one down.

member.remarks: The carried bits are the locomotion's and the turning bit. The first bit is the first-person clip having ended. The alternate fire key does nothing with a laser designator in hand, and otherwise resets the perfect-shot timer.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.SetUpperBody(System.Int32)
member.summary: Plays an upper-body mode: its body clips and its first-person clip (HumanPlayer_SetUpperBody, igi2 0x4BD2E0).
member.param: The mode, eCurrentUpperBody: 0 none, 1 stand, 2 and 3 on the move, 4 and 5 crouched, 6 and 7 firing, 8 to 10 the reload's start, loop and end, 11 putting the weapon away, 12 drawing it.

remarks.para: Mode 0 clears the upper body and the request with it. Any other notes the network. Standing or crouched, the upper body plays the stand state's clip through the weapon for modes 1 to 5, the fire state's for a primary shot, and the weapon's own clip for a secondary shot, a reload step, a put-away or a draw — a draw from its end backwards. Lying flat there is no upper body: the whole body plays the lying state's clip, or the weapon's lying reload, put-away or draw.

The first-person model then plays the matching clip: stand for 1, 4 and 5, move for 2 and 3, fire for 6 and 7 — a primary shot starting up to 0.175 s in, drawn from the run stream — the reload steps for 8 to 10, and the draw for 11 forwards and 12 backwards.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.RunIdle
member.summary: Idle, ready for the next action (HumanPlayer_RunActionIdle, igi2 0x4B3E40).

remarks.para: The upper body follows the mode the locomotion asks for, except that the two crouched modes swap without a new clip. The precision is re-aimed. A lock takes the zoom off and locks.

A spent throwable in hand — a proximity mine or the RPG-18 with nothing left to fire, or a grenade that went off — forces the next weapon in the cycle. A change asked for starts with the zoom taken off.
With a weapon in hand the fire keys fire () and the reload key reloads.
With nothing to change to, the activate key activates what the view has found ().
With nothing asked for, the drop key drops a weapon its type lets be dropped (). Not yet: the computer, whose screens the shell presents.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.TryFireFromIdle(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponItem)
member.summary: The idle state's fire branch, HumanPlayer_RunActionIdle (igi2 0x4B4067…0x4B4347).
member.returns: when the idle state goes no further this tick.

remarks.para: The activate key in a bomb area with the C4 in hand fires it. With neither fire key held the reload is checked. Otherwise the alternate key picks the secondary fire type; a fire type that uses ammunition with nothing loaded reloads when there is more carried, or fires empty — unless the weapon waits on the server. A slot with no fire type, the binoculars and the thermal goggles check the reload instead. A grenade with no delay is thrown when fire is held or its pin is still in. Anything else starts firing.
The reload check is the primary's: the reload key with less than a load in and more carried, or ammunition that never runs out, reloads.

member.remarks: One draw from the run stream picks one of the four changeweapon_0N sounds; it is drawn whatever is in hand, and the sound and the put-away play only for a weapon still carried. The weapon stops being ready, and the AI hears it handled (HumanPlayer_SendHandleWeaponAIEvent, a range of 20480).

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.SelectWeaponFromCategory
member.summary: Turns a weapon-category key into a weapon to change to (HumanPlayer_SelectWeaponFromCategory, igi2 0x4A0140).

remarks.para: The keys pressed this tick pick a category, the last in key order winning: 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 5, 10, then 8. The grenade key steps from the category of the weapon shown through grenades, flashbangs and smoke grenades, three tries, to the first with one carried.
The weapon is the next carried one of that category after the weapon shown, when that one is of the category, and otherwise the first; it goes into as its number.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.CheckBinoculars(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Raises or lowers the binoculars or the goggles on their key, HumanPlayer_CheckBinoculars (igi2 0x4B3950) in the single-player game.
member.param: Whether lowering them puts the weapon they were raised over straight back in hand.

remarks.para: Only with binoculars that may be put in hand, and only on a key's press. With the binoculars already shown and their key held, or the goggles and theirs, they are lowered: the weapon they were raised over goes back in hand, at once when forced and otherwise as a change asked for, and the zoom comes down.

Otherwise the goggles' key (with the binoculars' up) turns infrared on and puts the goggles in hand, and the binoculars' puts them in hand. Anything else that was shown is kept to go back to; the new one's zoom is fired at once, its trigger let go at the end of the tick, and the weapon left ready. Either way the weapon's precision is set again.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.EnterComputer
member.summary: The computer state, HumanPlayer_InitStateComputer: a mounted gun being worked is paused; the crouch's clip crouched, the lying one lying, the stand's standing, with the stand's upper body unless lying; the standing precision; the view and the body locked; and the computer opened.
member.remarks: The sound listener's move to the view is the audio's, not ported here.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.RunComputer
member.summary: HumanPlayer_RunStateComputer: the player stands its ground. A computer key turns to its screen, unless it is shown; that key again, a weapon key, the binoculars or the goggles, a quit asked for, a hit or death closes the computer.

remarks.para: The map's key turns to the map only while it is enabled; while it is not, it closes the computer from the objectives and does nothing from another screen. The next and previous weapon keys are spent either way.

Closing frees the view and the body; a slot the save screen chose becomes the one saved to and quick-loaded from; the computer closes and the body's impact stops. Binoculars raised before it are fired again, as they were; their key, or the goggles', raises them if they are not in hand. The legs then die, go back to a gun they were working, or to the stance's own state.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.Create(OpenIGI.Game.Ai.AiDifficulty)
member.summary: Readies the player for a mission: the single-player path of HumanPlayer_CreateHandler (igi2 0x4B8010).

remarks.para: Every collision is switched on. The locomotion starts in with no signal; its entry runs on the first tick. The player's health is the tuning's Max damage scale, seven tenths of it on normal and four tenths on hard, and the damage table is cleared with the single-player multipliers.

The rest starts empty: walking off, no jump wait, no activation lock, not swimming, no speed from the legs, and a movement scale of zero until the first delayed update sets it, so the first tick does not move the legs.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.RunDelayed
member.summary: The living player's end of the tick: the alive half of HumanPlayer_RunDelayedHandler (igi2 0x4B8A50).

remarks.para: The carried weapons slow the legs by up to half, and to half again while the jump wait runs. The posture's precision settles seven tenths of the way to its aim and the weapon's by the cross-hair damping. A zoom that may not be used now is left. The mission score's health is what is left of the maximum, in whole percent. The perfect-shot timer counts on, and the collision body is fitted to the posture. Then the body's animation controllers that step themselves do, and last the weapon's own end of the tick runs ().

First the scope sways with the breath (); after the zoom check the kit rattles and the player pants as it runs (, ). Not ported yet: the save and load slots, the cheat keys, the inventory toggle and the sector lookup.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.ExplosionHit(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ExplosionHit@)
member.summary: A blast reaches the player, HumanPlayer_ExplosionHitHandler (igi2 0x4BA330): it lands on the chest, as its chest's share, eased on the easiest difficulty and sharpened on the hardest, shakes the view with its nearness, and, if it did any damage, the player cries out and the view flashes red.

remarks.para: The player's size for the blast is a third of its model's radius and its root bone's distance from its origin. The shake is full within three times the blast's full range of the eyes and gone at nine times; it runs out over the blast's ninety ticks. A dead player is hurt and shaken, but does not cry out.
The original only answers while the player is active, which a player always is here.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.GetFireFrame(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Where the player's weapon fires from: HumanPlayer_WeaponGetParentParametersHandler (igi2 0x4BCEC0).

remarks.para: The view's position and orientation. With inaccuracy asked for and the player not still for a second (), the orientation is turned off true by the weapon's and the posture's settled precision together: two draws from the run stream, the first scaling the precision in degrees for how far, the second a whole turn for which way round, built as a rotation by those two angles and taken after the view's own (the view's orientation times it).

The copy-protection degrade factors scale both the timer and the precision by how long the game has run; in a genuine copy they are one (DEGRADE_PlayerPerfectShotTimer, DEGRADE_PlayerAccuracy, both 0x3F800000) and the scale drops out exactly. The view's override position is not ported.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.RunFireRegular
member.summary: The trigger held, HumanPlayer_RunActionFireRegular (igi2 0x4B5090).

remarks.para: Firing keeps the perfect-shot timer at nothing. A lock locks. The fire type's key up after the first tick lets go, unless the weapon waits on the server: the trigger stays unpulled, a last kick is taken, and the release state follows.

Otherwise the weapon's status decides. A shot that kicked is taken. An empty weapon ends the pull: with ammunition that never runs out it reloads where it stands; otherwise the trigger is let go and the weapon made ready, and once the first-person clip has played the empty state follows. Last, a fire type in the slot fires on the first tick — every tick for a laser designator — and the first tick is over.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.EnterThrowGrenade
member.summary: Starts a throw, HumanPlayer_InitActionThrowGrenade (igi2 0x4B4D60): not lying flat, where the player goes back to idle. The hold and the tick count start again, the primary fire type is the one thrown, and the upper body and the first-person model play the fire ( mode 7).

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.RunThrowGrenade
member.summary: One tick of a throw, HumanPlayer_RunActionThrowGrenade (igi2 0x4B4880).

remarks.para: On its eighth tick the pin is pulled (the secondary fire type), its trigger let go and the weapon left ready, with the primary the fire type again. At the clip's hold point, while the fire key is down, the first-person clip and the upper body stand still and the hold counts up, the first tick of it to the sound of the grenade handled; let go, they play on to the sound of the throw and the hold point is passed. The clip's throw trigger then fires the primary, which throws.

Held at the hold point until it went off in hand, or played past its throw with nothing more of it carried, the throw turns into a change: the next weapon of the cycle goes in hand and is drawn from its end backwards, the hold point forgotten. Once the first-person clip ends the primary's trigger is let go, the weapon is ready and the player idle.

remarks.para: Getting on, from the top: at the ladder's top vertex, 2.4 m down, facing it, six steps from the top, through getting on at the top. The target speed along the body's local X axis.
The most the X speed may change this tick.
member.remarks: HumanPlayer_MoveOnGround (igi2 0x4BEFB0): the world speed is taken into the body's frame with the orientation's transpose, each horizontal axis moves toward its target clamped to its limit, the local vertical is dropped, and the result goes back through the orientation. So the legs never push vertically; gravity and the ground do that.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.SteadyTurns
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the ground speed turns with the body, so turning while moving redirects the movement at once. Not retail, which leaves it pointing where it pointed: see .

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.CarrySpeedThroughTurn(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Matrix3f)
member.summary: Turns the ground speed with the body over the turn this tick made (), so it keeps its place in the body's frame as the body turns.
member.param: The body's orientation before the turn.

remarks.para: Retail keeps in the world's frame and Human_UpdateBody never touches it, so after a turn the old speed points off to the body's side, and HumanPlayer_MoveOnGround clears a side speed at only the strafe step a tick (63.6 running, against 890.7 of forward speed): a quick turn at a run slides the player a metre and a half sideways for half a second, and a steady turn faster than about four degrees a tick drifts like a car. The steps are the strafe keys' feel, not meant to undo a turn.

The speed is taken into the frame before the turn and put back out through the frame after it, on the ground only -- in the air the body's turn is the player's look, and a jump keeps the way it was thrown. Starting, stopping and changing keys still move at retail's steps.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.Step(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.X87Single,System.Single)
member.summary: A change clamped to at most a step either way, as HumanPlayer_MoveOnGround compares it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.AimPrecision(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2PrecisionType)
member.summary: Selects the posture precision a state aims for (HumanPlayer_SetWeaponPrecision, igi2 0x49F5F0).
member.remarks: Every locomotion entry ends the same way: with a weapon held, the ideal precision is the posture's own plus |turning speed| × turning modifier × 3; with none it is zero. The posture's own is one of the weapon's seven, or for a jump the jumping modifier plus the running one, and from a crouch the crouched walk's as well. The sum is formed unrounded and stored once, as the original's FPU does.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.Gaits
member.summary: The twenty-four directional gaits, from their entries and per-ticks: the runs, states 3–10 (HumanPlayer_InitStateRun* igi2 0x4A38B0–0x4A5CC0, RunStateRun* 0x4A39F0–0x4A5DE0), the walks, states 11–18 (0x4A61F0–0x4A84E0, 0x4A6320–0x4A85F0), and the crouched walks, states 26–33 (0x4A9480–0x4AB590, 0x4A9590–0x4AB6A0). Every number is the bit pattern of the original's constant.

remarks.para: The run rates are the HUMANPLAYER_RUN*_ANIMTIMESCALE globals at 0x63D764 — 1.0, the two side runs 1.2 — applied through . The walks never call it, so a walk plays at whatever rate its clip was left with.

Runs and walks also differ in their entry: a walk asks for upper-body action 2 and aims the walking precision, a run action 3 and the running one; and only the straight and side runs cut to their clip on landing from a jump.

The crouched walks share their exits with crouching still (see ), make no walk noise, and with their keys still held only check the water depth. Their phase-keeping sets are the original's, lopsided as they are: forward keeps the run's phase, backward the walk's.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.PickUpGun(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Pickups.Igi2GunPickupGrant@)
member.summary: Takes a weapon picked up: Human_GunPickupHandler (igi2 0x500180) over Human_PickupGun (0x4FFF20).

remarks.para: Only a living human with weapons takes one. A weapon not carried before is carried now, with the message that names it, and loaded and given its rounds (). One carried already only adds its rounds to what is carried of each fire type's ammunition, and, unless it is a weapon carried as rounds of itself, its load's worth to the first's as well. Either way the pickup sounds.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.Pickup
member.summary: Offers the player each of the level's pickups in turn, HumanPlayer_Pickup (igi2 0x49F8C0).

remarks.para: Not when dead, and no weapon while one is being changed or the binoculars are up. A weapon is taken outright when it is one already carried, which only adds its rounds, or when nothing of its category is: within reach, in sight, and not refused for carrying all its rounds already ().

A weapon of a category carried in another weapon is only offered: within reach, with nothing to activate in view, the action menu offers to swap it for each weapon of its category carried (HumanPlayer_RegisterWeaponPickupActionItem, 0x49F810). When the activate key goes down with that swap first on the menu, the weapon is taken and the one carried thrown down in its place, with its carried ammunition unless the two share it; the walk over the list ends there. Taking the one in hand asks for a change to the one taken.

remarks.para: A death goes to the end at once. A weapon change asked for takes the zoom off and changes. Otherwise, each time the loop's clip has played the player reloads, ending with fire held, with no more than one round carried, or one round short of a load, and looping again otherwise.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2HumanPlayer.Update
member.summary: One tick of the player: HumanPlayer_Update (igi2 0x4A1EC0).

remarks.para: The order is the original's, because each step reads what the one before left.

list.item: Off the ground, or hit, the next jump waits fifteen ticks; it counts down once landed.

Death is checked. A weapon-category key and the weapon cycle keys ask for a weapon change (the computer, which keeps the cycle keys for itself, is not ported). A locked activation clears the activate key.
Water is sounded: wading stirs it; past 819.2 the player cannot lie, past 3276.8 not crouch, and past 5734.4 the swimming bit is raised. The weapon is drawn unless swimming.
Ground steeper than fifty degrees takes the forward and back keys away, a held missile launcher forbids lying, and a computer page open blocks fire.
The locomotion states run, then the action states; the walk toggle flips on its key, and only standing can run.
The hit bit drops; the body turns, the view aims and, lying, is kept out of the ground.
The animation's step is scaled; on the ground the legs' own speed is added to it. The body moves, unless waiting for the network or flying; off the ground or dead the legs add nothing.

Lying, the body is re-noted on its platform. The main clip steps and the eyes are placed. A trigger the fire state pulled fires now, unless dead, and the perfect-shot timer starts again; the weapon lets go what the tick let go of (Weapon_UpdateStatus). The view's kicks die away.

remarks.para: Not ported yet: the action menu's pickups. The degraded-copy slowdown is inert: its factor is one.

member.summary: Keeps a lying player from looking into the ground or the roof: humanplayer.c HumanPlayer_CheckViewCollision (igi2 0x4BF340).

remarks.para: A point a reach ahead of the eyes along the body's forward axis is probed straight down and straight up, a reach of two each way. Each limit is the angle (Real32_Acos) between the body's forward axis and the line from the eyes to the surface struck. Ground below that faces up limits how far the view may look down, to minus that angle. A ceiling above that faces down limits how far it may look up, to the angle; ground above that faces up (a rise ahead) lifts the view to at least the angle.
Each limit that bites sets the aim, drops the kick, keeps the look input from pushing further the same way and aims the view again with what is left of it. Only a lying player is checked.

remarks.para: The clip plays at the rate the weapon gives it, negated to reverse, a frame's worth of ticks times that rate a step. A clip playing backwards starts that far before its end. The action signal's first bit, which the action states wait on, is cleared while the clip plays.
A weapon with no such clip leaves the model's clip ended and raises the bit at once, so whatever waits on it does not wait. With nothing in hand nothing happens.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2MovementCamera
member.summary: The orbiting camera of timed interactions (mode 3) and of the player's death (mode 5), humancamera.c's movement and death cameras: it circles the body's root, the mouse turning it, and is kept out of whatever it would enter.

remarks.para: Entering the mode (HumanCamera_MovementInit, HumanCamera_DeathCameraInit) looks for room around the body (computermap.c sub_4DE380): from the root, lines of 12288 — the ideal distance and two metres — at eight pitches in turn, eight headings at each from a quarter turn right, in the body's frame, against everything but the player; the first line that meets nothing, or water while looking down on it, is taken outright, otherwise the longest. The camera starts two metres short of where that line stopped.

Each tick (HumanCamera_UpdateAlphaAndGammaWithCollisions) the mouse turns it by up to six degrees a tick, its pitch held between −71.2° and 89°; it is placed on its orbit (sub_4DE620), then pushed out of anything near (sub_4DE830): twelve lines of two metres from it, along an icosahedron's corners, against everything, each one that strikes pushing it along the face's normal by what the line fell short, the pushes averaged. Its pitch, heading and distance are then read back from where it stands (sub_4DE720), the distance no more than the ideal, and it looks back at the root (sub_4DEE70). Only when nothing but the player's own body was struck does the distance move back toward the ideal, by a thirtieth of a metre a tick.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2PlayerAction
member.summary: The bindable player actions, as bits of the input port's 64-bit button words.

remarks.para: From the remap table GOInRemap resolves action names against (igi2 0x63EC88): forty-byte records of { char name[32]; u64 mask; }, grouped under TAB- headings the controls menu shows. config.qsc binds keys to these names (GOInRemap(MoveForwards, …, KEY_W)), so the names are the stable contract and the masks are where the port's button words put them.

The low dword is Input_s.bCurrentButton's low word, the high dword its high word; the edge word (pressed this frame) has the same layout. Multiplayer-only actions are listed for completeness: the single-player channel reader never looks at them.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2PlayerInputReader
member.summary: Fills a channel frame from the player's input, as HumanPlayerInput_ReadChannels does.

remarks.para: igi2 0x5296C0, the single-player path. The frame starts zeroed and each binding writes 1 or 0 to its channel; the look channels carry the analog deltas scaled by the profile's mouse sensitivity, clamped to [0.05, 1], with the turn keys nudging the horizontal one by 0.05 either way.

Most channels read the held word. The weapon-category selectors and the inventory read the pressed word, so holding a category key selects once; the computer pages and the stand/lie toggle read the held high word and leave the edge to the state machine's own last-tick test.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2PlayerTuning
member.summary: The player's tuning, read from humanplayer.qvm once at start-up.
member.remarks:
Flow_CreateHandler (igi2 0x401600) runs LOCAL:humanplayer/humanplayer.qsc into a HumanPlayerConfig task straight after the AI's settings, before any level: the script declares one HumanPlayerConfigItem, whose figures every player then takes (HumanPlayer_UpdateParameters, 0x4BD1F0). The task stays in the tree for the session.
The item also carries two scripts, evaluated as it takes its parameters (HumanPlayerConfigItem_UpdateInternalDataHandler, 0x438540): the weapon cycle's, which calls DefineHumanPlayerWeaponCycle, then the ammunition limits', which calls DefineHumanPlayerAmmoLimit. Both natives replace a global table; the limits apply to every human made afterwards, soldiers included.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Player.Igi2PlayerWeapons
member.summary: The player's weapon as its body and its input handling see it: the weapon in hand, out of the inventory.

remarks.para: Answers what the locomotion and the signal packing ask of the held weapon from the item the inventory has in hand (Weapon+0x2C): its category, its precision per posture (WeaponType+0x348…+0x368), whether its secondary fire type is a zoom (+0x528), whether it is a gun firing missiles, how much the carried weapons slow the player, and the clips it gives a body.

A weapon type keeps one clip table per rig it was built for (WeaponType+0x790/+0x794, WeaponType_GetAnimHeaderFromWeaponTypeAnim, igi2 0x4383B0); this builds a table the first time a rig asks for one and keeps it.
Firing is the weapon's own (), its fire types' handlers chosen by . Not yet: zooming and the overlay, and the sound slots; until then those requests do nothing, as they do with nothing held.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Saves.Igi2SaveGame
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's save games (savegame.c, serialize.c): a script that, run, puts the level's state back. It opens with SaveGameInfo(version, mission, ticks); and BreakScript();, which stops a run that only wants the header, then has a DefineTaskState call for each task that keeps state: the task found by its nearest ancestor with a level id and the types and places of the tasks between, then the task's own fields.

remarks.para: Serialize_SerializeHandler, from the root down: a task's children are written before it. A task with a level id is written against itself; one without, or one that is written with its parent, against the nearest ancestor that has one.

Serialize_DeSerializeScriptFunction: the ancestor is looked up by its id and checked against its type's name, and each step down is the child of that type at that place among its siblings of the type; a task that is not found is skipped. The fields are read in the order written ().
The retail game compiles the script to .qvm beside it; this game writes the script and reads either.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Scripting.Igi2GenericScripts
member.summary: The scripts most of I.G.I. 2's soldiers and squads run: a mind left to its type's default handler, and a squad left to its default, found in the installation itself.

remarks.para: I.G.I. 2 gives every soldier and every squad a compiled script of its own, MISSION:AI/<id>.qvm and MISSION:AI/Squad_<id>.qvm. Most are one script, byte for byte, which leaves every event to the AI's default handler (AIFunction_DefaultHandler, AISquad_DefaultHandler): 546 of the campaign's 1194 soldier scripts and 269 of its 471 squad scripts. A soldier another game's level places has no script of I.G.I. 2's, so it runs that one, as an ordinary I.G.I. 2 soldier does.
Read from the installation, so nothing that hosts I.G.I. 2's soldiers carries the game's files.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Scripting.Igi2LineScript
member.summary: Script text a task carries in a VarString parameter, evaluated as the original does: one expression.

remarks.para: A soldier's or the player's Weapon parameter and the player tuning's two Define ... script parameters are source text, not compiled code. Script_ParseLineInt32 (igi2 0x40D950) reads the text through SingleLine_GetInput (0x55E830), parses one expression from it (Expression_Parse, 0x558690) and evaluates that as an integer. The parser stops at the first ;, so whatever follows it never runs: Human_AddWeapon("A"), Human_AddWeapon("B"); gives both weapons, while Human_AddWeapon("A"); Human_AddWeapon("B"); gives only the first, and several of mission 1's soldiers are written the second way.

SingleLine_GetInput hands the parser a line at a time with everything from // to the line's end cut off, unless the // is inside a quoted string; there is no block comment. is that pass, and the expression language is then the shared one (), the same family as this game's.

member.remarks: SingleLine_GetInput (igi2 0x55E830): inside quotes a backslash skips the character after it.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier
member.content: Throwing a grenade, a close-combat blow, pressing a switch, a door, a silent death and a stand action.
The turn of the soldier's spine, shoulders and head toward what it aims at: the bone callbacks HumanSoldier_UpdateInternalDataHandler (igi2 0x4EB0F0) sets on its rig.

remarks.para: Each runs as the hierarchy reaches its bone, on the bone's orientation in the body's frame. The lower back finds the aim: the target less the body and the bone's parent, turned into the body's frame (straight ahead when there is none or it is less than a metre in front); its heading, held to sixty degrees, and its tilt are kept. With an upper-body clip playing it first replaces the parent's turn with the clip's own root key. Then it turns by half the heading about Z and by a share of the tilt about X; the upper back and the shoulders turn by the heading and their own shares of the tilt, and the head by the mind's head turn. Every quaternion product counts operations; past a thousand the quaternion is renormalised.
The sines are the FPU's own: some stored to a float before use, some used as they come, as each callback does.

member.summary: An enemy soldier's body, as I.G.I. 2's HumanSoldier_t runs it.

remarks.para: The soldier's own part over the shared body: its states, its upper body, and the fields HumanSoldier_t adds to Human_s. Its mind writes the same channel block the player's input does, read with the soldier's own meanings ().

A tick (HumanSoldier_RunHandler, igi2 0x4EA190) only queues the soldier for the delayed pass. There () the body's children run, its HumanAI among them, and the mind sends the update that moves the body.

member.content: How a soldier is struck: its collision, the zone a bullet finds, and the damage it takes.
Where a soldier's weapon fires from.
The soldier's flashbang response, humansoldier.c HumanSoldier_FlashBangHandler.
Flinching from a hit, and dying.
The soldier's locomotion states.
What a soldier's mind reads of its body and asks it to do.
Lying down, firing and reloading prone, a prone flinch and death, and lying dead.
Its save state as a human: its difficulty, how well it hits and how well it is seen are a soldier's own.
A soldier the player may kill silently: an enemy, alive and active, with the player's eyes behind it and near its line, and nothing between (HumanSoldier_EvaluateActivateHandler, igi2 0x4EBF10).
Manning a mounted gun.
Running tense in four directions, running in panic, and rolling aside.
The soldier's upper body: what its arms and weapon do over its legs' clip.

The clip's end stands it again, and so does a fall, a hit or a death, in that order of weight.
member.remarks: The clip's end outranks a fall, a hit and a death: a soldier killed as the throw ends stands first.

member.remarks: The state starts in , its entry run on the first tick; nothing in the signal. Walls do not stop a soldier (its mind keeps it to its graph), its ground is probed from 4096 above, it walks, flinches past a third of its life, and its upper body starts idle.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.Update(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Single})
member.summary: Takes the tick's channels and runs the soldier: HumanSoldier_HumanUpdateHandler (igi2 0x4EB250).
member.param: The channel frame the mind wrote, values.
member.remarks: A locked channel block keeps last tick's frame ().

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.Update
member.summary: One tick of the soldier's body: HumanSoldier_Update (igi2 0x4E3F50).

remarks.para: The locomotion states run, the walk toggle flips on its channel, the upper body runs and the hit bit drops. Then as for any human: the body turns, the view aims, the main clip steps, the body moves, the eyes are placed, and the weapon lets go what the tick let go of.
A soldier riding something (a mounted gun) is carried with it instead of moving (Human_Attach).
Last it tells the level's listeners where it is (Human_Notify): a mine before it is set off by a soldier too.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.RunDelayed
member.summary: The soldier's delayed half: HumanSoldier_RunDelayedHandler (igi2 0x4EA1B0), then the shared human's run handler with the body's children, its mind last.
member.remarks: The main clip steps a frame a tick again, the soldier is as visible as the light it stands in (less crouched or lying), its speed scale is one, and it takes the room its nodes place it in ().

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.Sector

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.UpdateSector
member.summary: Takes the room the soldier's graph nodes place it in: HumanSoldier_UpdateSector (igi2 0x4EA030).
member.remarks: Its mind's graph decides. Between two legal nodes, the first one's room -- unless the two lie in different rooms and the second is no farther from the body, when it is the second's. Otherwise the room of the node it is at. No graph, no room. The graph nodes carry their rooms from the level's load ().

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.MainTimeStepReset

member.remarks: The body's own bits are kept; the main and upper-body clips' ends and the walk toggle are read; then each channel raises its bit. An activation's channel holds the task to activate, taken once (not on a mounted gun); a weapon channel puts that weapon in hand.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.WeaponHit(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponHit@)
member.summary: A bullet striking the soldier, HumanSoldier_WeaponHitHandler (igi2 0x4EB290).

remarks.para: A dead soldier takes nothing. A live one takes the hit unless its mind keeps harm off it or its own side fired; then the zone is found () and the damage is the hit's times the zone's multiplier, except a knife's, and a head or groin hit where the mind keeps instant death off. The zone takes it, the total takes it, and it counts toward a flinch.

At the limit the soldier dies: its friends hear of it, and unless one hit took it all a death cry is raised; how and which way it died are kept and the dead bit is raised. Short of it the soldier flinches and cries out, and the AI hears it take damage. Unless one hit killed it, its mind says a line.
Blood is thrown once the damage is taken (). The shooter's tally counts the hit and the kill (, ). The knife's bruise is the renderer's.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.ExplosionHit(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ExplosionHit@)
member.summary: A blast reaching the soldier, HumanSoldier_ExplosionHitHandler (igi2 0x4EB8E0): none while its mind keeps harm off it or a human of its own side set it off; otherwise its view shakes with the blast's nearness to its eyes, and the blast lands on its chest at the chest's multiplier, measured from its eyes. It counts toward a flinch; at the limit the soldier dies of it (how it died nought, the shot's direction from the blast), else it cries out and flinches.
member.remarks: The soldier's size for the blast is a third of its model's radius and its root's distance from its origin, the root as the animation last left it. A kill counts to the blast's owner. Not yet: the soldier's isActive (Human+0x4A5), taken as set.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.CloseCombatDamage(System.Single,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2Human)
member.summary: A blow in close combat, HumanSoldier_CloseCombatDamageHandler (igi2 0x4EBCD0): to the chest when the soldier faces its attacker, else to the back, at that zone's multiplier. At the limit the soldier dies of it (how it died 4, the direction from the attacker); else it cries out and flinches. Unless its mind keeps harm off it.
member.remarks: Harmed or not, its friends hear a wounded cry from it, and its own mind is told the same (event 31, team 1, the attacker its reference and originator); the event's direction is left as the stack held it, so none is given.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.Say(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String})

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.HasFireFrame
member.remarks: A soldier fires from its mind's frame, so only one with a mind can.

remarks.para: HumanSoldier_WeaponGetParentParametersHandler (igi2 0x4E9B60): three draws of the run stream go unused first. The shot leaves from the mind's fire position (HumanAI+0x60) toward its aim point (+0x7530): the forward column is the unit direction, the side column that direction crossed with straight up (not normalised, so shorter the steeper the aim), and the up column the side crossed with forward, normalised.
With the aim point on the fire position, or straight above or below it, the mind's own orientation (+0xA0) is used. The inaccuracy flag is the player's: a soldier's frame takes none.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.EnterHit
member.summary: A flinch, HumanSoldier_InitStateHit (igi2 0x4E7CD0): a short clip drawn from three, or the zone's long one once the hits since the last flinch pass the threshold. A hit to the body or arms plays it on the upper body (the legs standing tense if upright); one to the legs plays it on the whole body, a kneeling soldier's from the kneeling clips, with the upper body tense over it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.RunHit(System.Boolean)
member.summary: A flinch's tick, HumanSoldier_RunStateHitLowerBody (igi2 0x4E7E70) and RunStateHitUpperBody (0x4E8040): off the ground it falls, dead it dies, hit again it flinches again, and once its clip ends it kneels or stands. A whole-body flinch waits on the main clip and keeps its upper body tense; an upper-body one waits on that clip.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.EnterDie
member.summary: A standing death, HumanSoldier_InitStateDie (igi2 0x4E8450): the weapon stops, the body stands upright, and the clip and the push it takes are chosen by how it died and which way the shot came.

remarks.para: How it died is nought for no weapon's hit yet ported: the soldier turns from the shot and falls one of two ways if it came from behind, or the third if from the front, pushed along it. By a shotgun likewise between two. By a gun, a head, chest or body shot from behind that did more than two damage throws it back three times in ten. Otherwise it plays the next of the shared eleven clips, a head shot one of the first three, pushed along the shot by a gun or a pistol.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2HumanSoldier.CycledDeath(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Humans.Igi2DamagePart,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f)
member.summary: The next of the shared death clips, a head shot's one of the first three, and its push.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Soldiers.Igi2ShootableSoldiers
member.summary: A level's I.G.I. 2 soldiers as another game's shots find them: the engine's humans among the world's colliders.

remarks.para: A round of another game is cast at each living soldier's own bone collider, as this game's trace meets it, and the struck soldier's task takes the hit, its bone carried for the zone ().

A soldier with a mind hears a round that passes within two metres of its head (Human_EvaluateGunShotHandler), one AIEVENT_GUNSHOTMISS from where it was fired, as it hears this game's bullets; a soldier of team one hears none, as this game's handler compares with the weapon's team.

member.summary: Makes a body for each of a level's soldiers, as Human_CreateHandler (igi2 0x4FDC90), HumanSoldier_CreateHandler (0x4E9E10) and Human_UpdateInternalDataHandler (0x4FF2F0) make one.
member.param: Builds a body's surroundings, weapon and animation for a soldier's task and rig.
Resolves a placed model name to its mesh.
The session's run stream, which every soldier draws from.
The model each soldier wears, its face given; for the level's own.
member.remarks: Each stands where the level puts it, turned by its Gamma and upright; its weapon script arms it. Its task runs it from then on (). Every soldier gets a collider over its model's posed mesh (), and they share one death clip counter.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2GuestContent
member.summary: What every I.G.I. 2 soldier another game's level hosts is made of, read once a session from the I.G.I. 2 installation: its tables, its packs' models and clips, its sounds and its generic scripts.

remarks.para: The packs are opened in I.G.I. 2's own order (Game_CreateHandler): the global common pack, new, then each location's pack that holds a model the host dresses a soldier in. A soldier's body is in its location's pack, the clips and the rigs in the common one.
The sounds are I.G.I. 2's common ones and those locations': its mission sounds are a level's own, and the level here is the host's.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2GuestLevel
member.summary: An I.G.I. 2 level of squads and soldiers hosted inside another game's level: its tasks made in a guest session of I.G.I. 2, then brought up as I.G.I. 2 brings its own -- the bodies, the detectors, the minds and the level's walk.

remarks.para: The host decides who stands where; this does what I.G.I. 2's own level build does with them, in its order (): the soldiers spawned (), the detectors listing them and the player, the minds given their scripts and graphs (), every human's AI events sent to the level's AI, and the level run that walks it.
Each guest task keeps the id the host asks for when the guest has not given it out, else the next spare id from the top: a mind finds its script by its id, and one without an id would run none.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2GuestLevel.AddAlarm(System.Int32,System.Func{System.Boolean},System.Nullable{System.ValueTuple{System.Int32,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Action}})
member.summary: Adds an alarm of the host's to the level, as I.G.I. 2's soldiers raise and hear their own: a control whose alarm is the host's, and, where the host's has one, a trigger where the host's is, which a soldier the squad sends presses (AISquad_TriggerAlarm).
member.param: The host's alarm control's id, which the squads that run for it name (AlarmControlId).
Whether the host's alarm is sounding this tick.

The host's alarm trigger: its id, which the squads press (AlarmTriggerId), where it is in world units, and what presses the host's own, as one of its guards presses it; for an alarm the soldiers only hear.
member.returns: Whether the alarm was added; not where an id is the guest's already.
member.remarks: The control's alarm expression reads the host's alarm, so as it starts and stops the control tells every soldier (AIEVENT_ALARMON, AIEVENT_ALARMOFF), as I.G.I. 2's own does, whoever raised it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2GuestLevel.AddPatrolPath(System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{OpenIGI.Game.Ai.AiPatrolCommand})
member.summary: Adds a patrol path to the level under the id the host gives it, which a soldier's script sends it on by (AIAction_Patrol): its commands in order, each as I.G.I. 2 keeps one.
member.param: Its commands, in the host's terms.
member.returns: The path; where the id is the guest's already, and no script could reach the path by it.
member.remarks: I.G.I. 2 reads a command's node, its delay or its animation from its Command Parameter (HumanAIContent_PatrolRunCB), as Project I.G.I. reads its operand, so each command keeps its kind and operand. An animation is the host's own number, which names nothing of I.G.I. 2's: it is a pause of about the length a retail patrol's animation takes instead ().

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2HostedLevel
member.summary: An I.G.I. 2 squad level running inside another game's level: its soldiers standing in for the host's humans, run where the host's walk reaches them, seen, struck and drawn as the host's own.

remarks.para: Each soldier stands for a host human (): it is in the world while that human's task is, as the host's containers put it in and take it out, and the host's task dies with it -- the latch the host's scripts read. A host generator spawns its later lives from a pool made with the level ().

A tick of the level is its walk's, then what follows the world: what the host has it do each tick, the soldiers in and out of the world, the player's visibility for the next tick's detection, and the soldiers' sounds once, as the game runs its own.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Systems.Igi2LevelSystems
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's level systems, in the order its level is brought up.

remarks.para: The order is the original's load: the tree's update and after-load handlers, which run task by task in the tree's order, gathered here by what they are about. What later systems read is made by earlier ones -- the sectors and the listener by , what the detectors see by , the mounted guns and cars by their systems before the AI looks them up, every list of things to activate and to move before and -- and the level's random streams are drawn from in this order, so it is part of the simulation.
A mod edits 's list by these names.
