member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2Task
member.summary: A task of I.G.I. 2's level tree: the root of every type the title gives a class, as QTask is the root of the original's types.

remarks.para: The original declares each type with a parent (QTask_NewQTaskType(name, size, parent)) and copies the parent's handler table into it, so a type that links no handler of its own for an event answers it with its parent's. The title's classes follow the same tree, and an event handler is a virtual member here: a class overrides the handlers its retail type links and inherits the rest.
A parameter list is inherited only where the original derives one (ParameterList_Derive); such a class carries .

It is a , the shared base, so the shared level run reaches it as it reaches any typed task; its run handler takes I.G.I. 2's run, whose script functions, cutscene camera and sector portals the title's handlers read.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2Task.Run(OpenIGI.Game.Level.LevelRun)
member.remarks: In I.G.I. 2's own level run the task's run handler runs, reading that run's state. Any other title's run sees it as it sees a type it has no class for, a container whose children it walks: the host still walks an I.G.I. 2 level with the first game's cutscene runtime, which finds nothing of its own in it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Igi2Task.Run(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Flow.Igi2LevelRun)
member.summary: Runs the task one tick: its run handler (event 1).
member.remarks: The base type links no run handler, so a task that does not override this does nothing, and neither do its children: the run pass is not a walk, a task's children run only when its own handler runs them.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarAiTask
member.summary: A car's driver, I.G.I. 2's CarAI (carai.c, an EditBoneObj): it follows its patrol route over its AI graph, chases what its car's gun sees, and drives the car through its steering, thrust and brake.

remarks.para: CarAI_RunHandler, after its children: its route is started the first time; then, while its car, its graph, and a route or a fight are there, it drives. Its driving expression, where it has one, says whether it is at the wheel. Dead, or not at the wheel, it stops: no speed and full brake. In a fight it heads for the graph node nearest what it saw, and once there turns on the spot to aim the car at it. On its route it carries out the route's commands: to a node it drives (at the speed last set), a delay it waits out braked a tick at a time, a speed it sets, an expression it waits for, and an end or a quit stops it; anything else it passes over. Then the car is driven a tick (CarAI_UpdateCar).

Its way to a node is an A* path over the graph (CarAI_MakePath), from whichever end of the edge it is on is nearer the node; it heads for each node of the path in turn, reaching one when it is within three metres across and eight along the car, or three metres round in a fight (CarAI_IsOnNode). Its speed is the target speed where the way runs straight on and five where it turns square (CarAI_FindWantedSpeedPatrol); its thrust closes on that speed a hundredth at a time, braking when it is three over (CarAI_FindWantedThrust); and it steers full lock past ten degrees off, less the more thrust it has.

member.content: Its save state, CarAI_ptSerializeParameterList: its route's command and its last end, by level id, whether its driver is dead and its damage, its tick, its way over its graph, and the speed its route last set.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask
member.summary: A car, I.G.I. 2's Car (car.c, a Vehicle): a physics object on sprung wheels that its CarAI drives, which may carry an automatic gun, and which blows up when a rocket reaches it.

remarks.para: Car_RunHandler, once a tick: its engine sound, made of its type's sound while its play sound expression holds (or always, with none) and deleted when it does not; its open door expression, given to its door; its detection, while its can fire expression holds, from its gun's muzzle along the gun; its children (its driver, who drives it); its kill boxes, while it is not at rest; its gun mounted where the car now is, and run; then its explosion, if one is coming.

It moves only when its driver drives it (Car_UpdateAnimDataHandler): a step at tick nought sets it back where the level put it, at its original thrust; any other step takes the thrust (unless it is -1), the steering and the brake (a fourth channel other than -1), and moves it a tick ().

Car_Explode: a car with no explosion vertices goes off once at its centre, a quarter of its radius at full damage; one with them goes off at each, each a random number of ticks below thirty later. Ten or thirty ticks on, it is taken out of the world, its gun and its sound with it, and its destroyed model is left where it stood.

member.content: How a car moves (Car_Move): its thrust and steering come round by their inertias; its wheels' springs hold it up and its driven wheels push it, each wheel rubbing along the ground as it is steered; its wings meet the air; and the physics object takes a tick under a gravity of 44.6 units a tick squared, keeping 0.97 of its speed and 0.9 of its spin.
Its save state, Car_ptSerializeParameterList: a model object's, then its velocity and its direction, whether it has blown up, and its thrusts.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask.AddSpringForces(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject,OpenIGI.Game.Physics.CarTypeDefinition,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsWorld)
member.summary: The springs, Car_AddSpringForces: each wheel that is there and has a contact point traces a line down through it, from a metre above where its spring would be fully compressed to half a metre below the point; its contact point stops meeting the world for itself. Ground struck within the spring pushes up at the point by how far it is compressed over its reach, times its stiffness, the car's mass and the gravity; ground above the spring's reach pushes harder the further above, and lifts the car out by the most any wheel is in. Either way the wheel touches, where its contact point is lifted 0.4 m, and drives and rubs. A wheel that is not there leaves its point to meet the world.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask.AddWheelForces(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject,OpenIGI.Game.Physics.CarTypeDefinition,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: A wheel's push and rub, Wheel_AddForces: a driven wheel touching while the car has thrust (or any driven wheel of a car held level) pushes along the ground, in the car's forward direction laid on it, by the thrust its share of the engine gives less the car's speed, turned by the wheel's steering; a crawler's track pushes less on the inside of a turn. A touching wheel then rubs (), across by its point's first friction and along by its second, or by its first both ways while the car brakes, which also takes a twentieth of its thrust.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask.AddFriction(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: A wheel's rub, Wheel_AddFriction: the point's velocity off the ground's plane, made a unit direction and taken into the car's frame, is turned into the wheel's (by its steering), scaled across and along by the two frictions and turned back. Slow enough to be held by the load on the wheel, the rub is that direction by the speed, the mass and a tenth; otherwise by the load and 0.24.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask.CrawlerScale(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject,System.Int32)
member.summary: How hard a crawler's track pushes in a turn, Wheel_GetCrawlerSpeedScale: turning one way, the tracks of contact points of the first kind push less; turning the other, those of the nought kind; going straight, all fully.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2CarTask.ApplyAirResistance(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Physics.Igi2PhysicsObject,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{OpenIGI.Game.Physics.Wing},OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f)
member.summary: The wings, Wing_ApplyAirResistance: the wind taken into the car's frame, its length squared by the coefficient; each wing with area is pushed along its normal by how squarely the wind meets it, its area, and that.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2DeathZone
member.summary: A vehicle's kill box, I.G.I. 2's DeathZone (deathzone.c): a magic object on the vehicle's attach point that kills the humans inside it while the vehicle moves.

remarks.para: DeathZone_RunHandler, single player only: while its car is not at rest, or its train has speed, every human is tested (Human_DeathZoneHitTestHandler).

An active human whose root bone is within the box's radius of its centre, and from whose root bone a line to the centre meets nothing of the box, is inside it: it takes ten thousand damage to the chest when the vehicle moves at fifty units a tick or more, none slower, and dies if that is enough.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Vehicles.Igi2TrainTask
member.summary: A locomotive or a carriage, I.G.I. 2's Train (train.c): a Vehicle that rides the spline its RailroadQTaskID names, at a distance along it, its carriages its child Train tasks, each hung a coupling's length behind the one in front. An AnimTask drives it; on its own it does not move.

remarks.para: Train_UpdateInternalDataHandler: its length is the distance between its model's first two magic vertices, its couplings; a locomotive is placed (Train_Move). Train_UpdateAnimDataHandler: channel nought, unless minus one, is the thrust it heads for. At tick nought it is set back: at its authored distance, its thrust and speed its original thrust's, and placed. At any other tick its thrust closes on the one it heads for by its acceleration, its speed is its thrust of its top speed in km/h, it moves that far along the spline, backwards when flipped, and is placed.

Train_RunHandler, once a tick: while its sound expression holds, it plays train_loop_1, or train_loop_2 with no carriages; its sound's two channels are its thrust (its locomotive's, for a carriage) five times over, held to between 0.8 and 1, and whether that thrust is over a thousandth; its children run.

member.content: Its save state, Train_ptSerializeParameterList: a model object's, then its thrusts, its speed and its place on its rails.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.ViewModel.Igi2AttachedParts
member.summary: The models a clip's attach objects hang on the bones of a posed body.

remarks.para: The clip's attach objects stand on their bones at their relative positions, moved by every re-link the clip has passed. A record's matrix turns its object as ModelObj_CreateAttachObject (igi2 0x56D0B0) reads it, its first two columns as rows and the third row their cross product; a re-link's matrix is taken whole and transposed (AnimController_Step, 0x5549A0). The object then stands at the bone's orientation times that (ModelObj_UpdateAttachment, 0x56CB40: parent · bone · relative).

One named weapon draws the weapon in hand's Fixed Model, as WeaponMagicObj_GetModelName (0x4733B0) finds it through the human that owns the body, and nothing when nothing is held; any other draws the model it names.

member.summary: What the view holds as one tick left it: the first-person model's pose and the models its clip hangs on it.

remarks.para: The view's clip is sampled as its controller is made to (HumanView_CreateHandler, igi2 0x4D5A30, sets the spline bit), so rotations are SQUAD-interpolated, and posed on the model's own hierarchy (BoneDynCubeObj_UpdateHierarchy, 0x564B50).
The clip's attach objects hang their models on the pose (), the weapon one the weapon in hand.

Nothing is drawn while the view is zoomed or its owner is dead, as HumanView_EnterHandler (0x4D5DB0) declines then. Not yet: an attach object's own key track, the grenade pin and the rocket, which have handlers of their own.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2AiStationaryGun
member.summary: An automatic gun, I.G.I. 2's AIStationaryGun (aistationarygun.c): a magic object on its carrier's attach point, whose head turns and whose barrel tilts towards the first enemy its carrier's detection sees, firing once it is on target.

remarks.para: AIStationaryGun_RunHandler: the first enemy listed with any point in plain sight is the target, its shoulders for a human, taken into the gun's frame: its bearing and its elevation are where to aim. A target lost is aimed at where it was for ninety ticks more; with none, the gun comes back to nought. Wholly turning guns go the short way round. The tilt and turn each move at most their speed a tick towards the aim, the turn kept within a half turn either way, then held within the gun's limits. With a target, within five degrees on both is on target: an empty weapon reloads, and on target it fires and its barrel spins. A trigger held as it comes off target, or a burst done, is let go. While the aim, held within the limits, is more than two degrees away, its rotation sound plays.
Its carrier places it, AIStationaryGun_UpdateAttachmentHandler: a holder once, a car each time it moves.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2AiStationaryGunHolderTask
member.summary: An automatic gun's holder, I.G.I. 2's AIStationaryGunHolder (aistationarygunholder.c): a model that carries an on its attach point and watches through a cone from the gun's muzzle while its on expression holds.
member.remarks: AIStationaryGunHolder_RunHandler: its team and on expressions, where it has them, set its side and whether it watches. member.summary: The damage a blast does a target, GameFunctions_ResolveExplosionHit (igi2 0x48D1F0): full within the full range of the target's edge, falling away over the falloff past it, and lessened by what lies between.
member.param: The target, which the line passes, or .
member.remarks: A timed action's object is not traced. The line, a weapon's, passes the target and the blast's owner. The line between runs 409.6 units above both. The blast starts with the full range over 4096 of penetration and loses each face's material's penetration power; stopped short, it does nothing. A target of no size or a blast of no range is not traced.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2FireHandlers
member.summary: Which handler each fire type has, as its task type registers them (Weapon_eFireQTaskEvent, Weapon_eReleaseQTaskEvent).

remarks.para: A fire type is the parameters task in its weapon's slot, and the weapon finds its handlers through that task's type (QTask_aatQTaskFinalEvent[Weapon_eFireQTaskEvent][type], Weapon_SingleFireHandler, igi2 0x51CD40). A type without one fires nothing: the weapon gives up before it spends, delays or kicks.

Ported: the Gun (Gun_Open, igi2 0x4835E0), the FireMode (FireMode_Open, 0x51BE60), the Zoom (Zoom_Open, 0x525DA0), the Knife (Knife_Open, 0x4CF970), the PullPin (PullPin_Open, 0x4C80C0) and the ProjectileLauncher (ProjectileLauncher_Open, 0x526E20), the designator, the proximity and remote mines, the medipack and the laser sight's switch. C4 is not: no single-player mission hands it out.

member.returns: The handler for a fire type's parameters task, or for a type with none.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2FireModeFire
member.summary: What a FireMode does when fired: FireMode_WeaponFireHandler (igi2 0x51BE00).
member.remarks: The secondary fire key on a weapon whose second slot is a fire mode steps the weapon in hand to its next fire mode, wrapping after its Available FireModes. The single-player game steps it only while the weapon is ready (status 0, Weapon+0x38); the hold time it tests is the multiplayer game's. It fires nothing, so it spends, delays and kicks nothing, and it has no release.

member.content: The weapon's two fire types and what they fire.
member.summary: One weapon, as WEAPONS/weapon.qvm declares it: WeaponType (WeaponType_Open, igi2 0x436C60).

remarks.para: The parameters are the script's own declaration, in wire order (Task_DeclareParameters in WEAPONS/weapon.qvm). Its children are the fire types Primary Fire TaskType and Secondary Fire TaskType name, and parameter containers of tagged values.
Weapon Type is the family a body borrows clips from (), and Weapon Animation Name the name its own clips carry ().

member.param: 0 for the primary fire type, 1 for the secondary.

member.summary: A tick of the grenade, Grenade_RunHandler (igi2 0x484260).
member.param: What its end shows and does.

remarks.para: While its fuse burns it counts down and moves (Grenade_Move, 0x483FE0): unless at rest, its physics object takes a tick under the grenade's gravity and damping.

An ordinary grenade tells the AI of itself on every fifth tick of its fuse. A contact at the last move sounds the bounce, which an ordinary grenade tells the AI of too, once until ten ticks go by without one.

The tick the fuse is out, the ground under it is probed and, for an ordinary grenade, the explosion goes off with the launcher's parameters, and the grenade is gone. Smoke keeps moving until its plume has faded.

member.summary: Works out the throw from a launch, Grenade_CreateProjectileHandler (igi2 0x484BE0), with the client's FPU arithmetic.
member.param: The launch: the fire's position and orientation, the fire type's speed and the fuse.

remarks.para: The throw's strength follows how high the fire points. Its first angle is folded onto the upper half turn, measured from straight down in half turns, and held between none and the ideal angle (in half turns too); its share of the ideal, raised to the gamma exponent, scales the speed, which becomes world units a tick. The grenade flies along the fire's forward column at that speed, plus the thrower's own.
The power is taken at double precision and then cut to the FPU's 24 bits: exact for the shipped exponent of one.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2GunFire
member.summary: What a Gun does when fired and let go: Gun_WeaponFireHandler (igi2 0x482740) and Gun_WeaponReleaseHandler (0x483490).

remarks.para: A round is the gun's bullets per round, or, counting bullets as rounds, no more than are loaded. Each bullet is a projectile of the gun's projectile type; when a round has more than one, each is turned off the line of fire by two draws from the run stream, an angle round the line and a distance out to the gun's spread. The gun reports one round fired, or every bullet when bullets count as rounds, and a delay of its rounds per minute in ticks.

The kick is two more draws, up and sideways, scaled by how far into the pull the gun is. A loud gun (an AI detection range past 20480) is heard far and keeps its holder visible for fifteen ticks; every shot tells the AI. Held by a drawn weapon object and not through a scope, it flashes, lights its holder, and, with a casing model, throws out a casing at a drawn angle with a drawn spin. The fire sound plays at the start of a pull: looped for full automatic, as a sequence ending in the tail for a burst.
The kick's attack curve is the C runtime's pow, which the FPU's precision reaches inside; it is taken here in double precision and truncated after. Nothing else in the handler depends on it.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2GunShot
member.summary: The shots a weapon fires as bullets, its GunShot task: fired this tick, traced this tick, gone by the next.

remarks.para: Weapon_CreateHandler (igi2 0x51C320) makes one under every weapon. The gun's fire handler hands each bullet to (GunShot_CreateProjectileHandler, 0x4C78A0), and the shot's run handler, which the scheduler calls straight after the human's because it is the weapon's child, traces them all in (GunShot_RunHandler, 0x4C76E0; GunShot_RunInstant, 0x4C6B50).

A bullet is traced from its muzzle to the end of its range against the forests, the solid models, the splines, the humans and the ground, one face at a time. At a face it goes into it does its damage, falling off by up to 30% over its range and in proportion to the penetration it has left, and hands the hit to what it struck; the ground stops it. The first face that makes a sound for the whole tick also makes the AI hear the strike. Every face it crosses takes the material's penetration power from it, and it stops when it has none left. A face it comes out of only costs it penetration. Up to ten faces leave an effect, all made once the bullet is done.
Before the trace every human weighs the bullets (): a soldier hears those that pass within two metres of its head ().

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2GunShotEffect
member.summary: What a bullet leaves on a face it crossed, GunShotEffect_CreateEffectHandler (igi2 0x520680): chips, a splash, a hole and smoke, with the run-stream draws they take.

remarks.para: A body, any boned object, gets neither chips nor smoke: its flesh is the human's own effect. Otherwise an effect that throws chips draws once for one or two fragments and starts an Explosion0 of no damage, which draws three angles of its own (Explosion0_NewEx, 0x50A650). Water then splashes and nothing more happens. Anything else takes a hole where it has holes, the penetrating one if the bullet went on and the effect names one; and an effect that smokes draws once more and, on an odd draw, raises two puffs from four further draws.
The Explosion0 then runs as any explosion does, its fragments flying, and drawing, over the ticks after.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2HumanWeapons
member.summary: How a human comes to carry weapons: its inventory, and the script that fills it.

remarks.para: Every human makes its inventory when it is made, limited by the player tuning's ammunition limits (Human_CreateHandler, igi2 0x4FDC90). Once the level is loaded, a human whose Weapon parameter holds script text has it evaluated with three natives pointed at that inventory and released after (Human_UpdateInternalDataAfterCarryoverHandler, 0x4FF440): Human_AddWeapon, Human_AddAmmo and Human_AddAmmoForWeapon, registered by Human_Open (0x504710).
The text is evaluated as a single expression (), so a script that ends its first call with ; adds only that one weapon.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ImpactGrenade
member.summary: A grenade fired from a launcher that bursts on what it strikes, ImpactGrenade: it flies under its own gravity, trailing smoke, and the first thing its path meets sets it off.

remarks.para: Fired (ImpactGrenade_CreateProjectileHandler, 0x4CC8B0) along the shot's forward column at the gun's speed, metres a second made units a tick; the shooter both made it and is passed over by its path.

Each tick (ImpactGrenade_RunHandler, 0x4CC2F0) its speed keeps 0.995 of itself, after 35.68 more of fall, and it moves by it; the line from where it was to where it is goes as a weapon's does. Struck, it goes off where it struck: one blast of its damage, full over its radius and falling away over as much again, three fragments and a fireball, explo_proxy, and AI event 20 heard 75 metres off; and it is gone. Otherwise its trail takes a puff, three draws of the run stream.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2Inventory
member.summary: What a human carries: every weapon and every ammunition the session defines, each marked carried or not.

remarks.para: The original's Weapon task, which every human makes for itself (Human_CreateHandler, igi2 0x4FDC90): Weapon_CreateHandler (0x51C320) lists one item for each ammunition type and one for each weapon type, in the order the session made them, and carrying a weapon is that item marked active. Weapons and ammunition are found by the name of their constant, compared exactly (Weapon_GetWeaponTypeItemFromWeaponType, 0x51E560, and Weapon_GetAmmoTypeItemFromAmmoType, 0x51E690), which is how the natives that fill it name them.
Multiplayer's branches are not here: the single-player campaign never takes them.

member.param: The name of its constant, WEAPON_ID_*.
Whether to add a load of ammunition with it.

remarks.para: A weapon newly carried starts with one round loaded in a fire type that must be loaded before it fires and none in the others. Asked for ammunition, it is then given one full load for each fire type (WeaponType_CalcGunPickupAmmo, 0x438330, with a fraction of one) through .

remarks.para: The weapon put away is dropped from the inventory when it was thrown or laid and none of it is left: a grenade or a proximity mine with no rounds carried, or an RPG-18 with none carried and none loaded either.
The new weapon starts ready, with no delay, no pin out, no fuse and no bullets fired. The zoom of the weapon put away is the firing's (), which comes here.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2KnifeFire
member.summary: What a Knife does when fired: Knife_WeaponFireHandler (igi2 0x4CF8A0) and Knife_Stab (0x4CF400).

remarks.para: The knife's traces are fanned across its trace field of view, centred on the aim, from left to right; each is a two-metre line from the shot's position along the aim turned by its angle, against everything. The first that strikes something stops the sweep: a human sounds a stab for a knife-kind weapon, or one of two punches by a run-stream draw for anything else, and any other surface its material's knife sound; then what was struck takes the knife's damage factor along the line.
It fires no rounds, waits its delay in ticks, kicks the view a hundredth of a degree both ways and damps it by a tenth, and plays its fire sound in the fire sound's slot.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2Missile
member.summary: A missile in flight, Missile_s: a physics object pushed by its motor, steadied by its fins, steering as its type says, and set off by the first thing it touches.

remarks.para: Fired (Missile_New, igi2 0x52F1D0) as its weapon's Missile - Model, along the shot's forward column at the gun's speed, its thrust full, its fuel its type's; a missile that steers straight aims four thousand metres ahead.

Each tick (Missile_RunHandler, 0x52E620, and Missile_Move, 0x52DB70): it steers, smokes while it has fuel, turns by its smoothed pitch and turn rates, wobbles once its fuel is out, is pushed by its motor while it has fuel and burns some, takes the air on its fins and moves as a physics object whose touch a weapon's line would make. Touching anything it goes off where it is, over what lies under it; and every thirty-two ticks one with nothing at all beneath it is gone.
Its wobble and smoke draw from the missiles' own stream (Missile_tRandomState), never the run stream. The sound it flies with is the presentation's.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ProjectileLauncherFire
member.summary: A fire type that throws or launches something of its own, ProjectileLauncher: ProjectileLauncher_WeaponFireHandler (igi2 0x526B40) and ProjectileLauncher_WeaponReleaseHandler (0x526CD0).

remarks.para: One that does not create on release creates its projectile as it fires: from the fire's position and orientation, at the fire type's speed, inheriting the thrower's, with the fuse of a pin already pulled or else the fire type's own Explode Time, thirty ticks a second. The pin goes back and the fuse with it, one round is taken, the next waits out the fire type's rate, and the fire sound plays in the weapon's second slot; the view takes a hundredth of a degree of kick each way, damped by a tenth.
Letting go fires nothing for such a fire type. Not yet: one that creates on release, which no shipped grenade is.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ProximityMineFire
member.summary: Laying a proximity mine: proximitymine.c ProximityMine_WeaponFireHandler; or, in its remote mode, RemoteMine_WeaponFireHandler, which lays one that no passer-by sets off and sounds nothing.

remarks.para: A line goes out along the aim for the fire type's effective range, against everything a weapon may strike. A surface it meets takes the mine, unless it is a human, glass, a door or a vehicle: the mine lies where the line struck, its Y axis the surface's normal (), the weapon's fixed model, arming after its time and set off by a human within its radius in front of it (). Laying it uses a round, waits a round's time and plays the fire sound in the fire sound's slot.
Laid or not, the view kicks a hundredth of a degree each way, damped by a tenth.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2StationaryGunTask
member.summary: A mounted gun, I.G.I. 2's StationaryGun (stationarygun.c): a holder that turns about its mount, a barrel of its weapon's fixed model that tilts, and a Weapon of its own with a load of ammunition, worked by whoever activates it from behind.

remarks.para: StationaryGun_UpdateInternalDataHandler: its weapon is its Weapon ID, with ammunition; an Ammo of minus one never runs out, otherwise it carries that much and no more, and is loaded.

StationaryGun_RunHandler, once a tick: its precision eases two fifths of the way towards its weapon's standing precision; its kick dies away by the weapon's damping. Worked, its tilt and turn follow the operator's look channels, a half turn a unit, held within its limits; the fire channel fires its weapon, and its letting go lets the trigger go; the kick throws an operator without an AI off; a tenth of the kick is shed. Not worked, the barrel droops towards nine tenths of its lowest tilt five degrees a tick. Then the holder is turned and the barrel placed (StationaryGun_PositionWeapon), and the weapon's status settled.
StationaryGun_Fire: a shot fired this tick adds two fifths of the weapon's kick, in degrees, to the precision, and the kick, in radians, to the gun's.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponTypeAnim
member.summary: A weapon type's own answer to a clip request, WeaponType_GetAnimHandler (igi2 0x4360F0).

remarks.para: The first-person stand and move are its named clips on the asking rig, at their own speed (Hierarchy_GetAnim, 0x57F360, looks a name up in one rig's clips). The first-person draw and put-away are its named clips too, played so that the whole clip lasts the weapon's (De)Activate Time: the clip's seconds (its ticks times the float 1/4800) over that time. The third-person stand, walk, run and crouched clips are named the same way.

The third-person draw and put-away come from the body's weapon table instead (WeaponType_GetAnimHeaderFromWeaponTypeAnim, 0x4383B0): rows 0xE9–0xEC, the standing and lying weaponraise, scaled the same way unless the time is zero.

Everything else is the fire type's to answer, as is any request this finds no clip for: the request goes on to the handler of the fire type in the asker's fire-type slot, when there is one. The gun's, the knife's, the pin's (PullPin_GetAnimHandler, 0x4C7FD0) and the launcher's (ProjectileLauncher_GetAnimHandler, 0x526960, whose last round throws with its Last clips) are ported; the other fire types' are not yet, and find none.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponTypeAnim.GunAnim(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2GunTask,OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponAnimRequest,System.Func{System.String,OpenIGI.Formats.Animation.Igi2AnimationClip},System.Func{System.Int32,OpenIGI.Formats.Animation.Igi2AnimationClip})
member.summary: A gun's answer, Gun_GetAnimHandler (igi2 0x4822E0): its named shot, held shot and release at their own speed, and its reload's three steps all at one rate, the one at which the whole reload (the start, a loop for every round of the clip but one, and the end) lasts the gun's Reload Time.
member.remarks: The first-person steps are the gun's named clips; the start counts the loop and the end only when the gun names a first-person loop. The third-person steps are the body table's reload rows (0x4F to 0x51, lying 0x7A to 0x7C), the start again counting the rest only for a named first-person loop. A missing step adds nothing. Each clip's ticks become seconds by the float 1/4800, the loop's times the rounds less one, summed in the handler's order and divided by the reload time at the FPU's precision.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponConstants
member.summary: The script constants the weapon scripts are written against, with the values the engine registers.

remarks.para: Every value is read from the call that registers it in igi2.exe: WeaponType_Open (0x436C60) for the categories, the weapon types, the sights and the ammo displays, AmmoType_Open (0x43B080) for the undefined ammo id, and HumanAI's registration (0x45CC42–0x45CC99) for the gunshot hearing ranges the weapons name. Several names share a value on purpose: the explosive, RPG and other categories are all registered as zero, as are the crosshair and circle sights.

A TASKTYPE_* constant is the id of the task type it names, which is what the engine compares it with when it makes a weapon's fire types. Here that is the id this session's registry gives the type; retail's own ids are its own registration order and nothing in a script depends on their numbers. TASKTYPE_NONE is the exception, a fixed 512 beyond every type.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring
member.summary: The firing half of a human's Weapon task: the trigger, the shot, the delay and the kick.

remarks.para: A shot starts in (Weapon_Fire, igi2 0x51DE90), which decides whether the trigger may fire at all, asks the holder where it fires from with the holder's inaccuracy, and sends the shot to itself as a message: the position narrowed to whole centimetres and the orientation to three angles. The single-player campaign hands the message straight to Weapon_SingleFireHandler (0x51CD40), which checks the ammunition and the delay, rebuilds the position and orientation, runs the fire type's own handler, and spends what it fired.

Held fire is the weapon's: once its first shot has fired an automatic weapon fires again every tick in (Weapon_RunDelayedHandler, 0x51C480) until its rounds in succession run out or the trigger comes up, and a burst let go early completes itself. The trigger comes up at the end of the holder's tick in (Weapon_UpdateStatus, 0x51E370).
The status, the delay, the pin, the fuse and the bullets fired are the inventory's (they share Weapon_s); what fires, shows and sounds is the fire type's handler and the .

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.Fire(System.Int32)
member.summary: Pulls a fire type's trigger, Weapon_Fire (igi2 0x51DE90).
member.param: 0 for the primary fire type, 1 for the secondary.

remarks.para: Nothing fires with nothing in hand, a holder that cannot say where it fires from, or no fire type in the slot. Nothing loaded leaves the weapon empty. A fire mode that fires a set number of rounds a pull waits out its delay (a zoom does not), fires only once a pull when that number is one or for the secondary fire type, and locks once the pull has fired them all.

The pull's first shot marks the trigger down at this tick; a grenade held by the player backdates it by the time held, and the mark is then the primary's whatever was pulled. The trigger's held time is the difference of the two ticks' low bytes. The holder's frame is taken with its inaccuracy.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.RunDelayed
member.summary: The weapon's end of the tick, after its holder's: Weapon_RunDelayedHandler (igi2 0x51C480).

remarks.para: The delay counts down. A pulled grenade's fuse burns: at nothing it goes off in hand, firing the primary and letting its trigger go, and every thirtieth tick before that it ticks.

A weapon firing on by itself fires again, and so does one finishing a burst; the shot is the primary's, with the held time of the fire type last fired and the holder's inaccuracy. Once the fire type last fired has nothing loaded or has fired its rounds in succession it stops: the trigger is let go and its count starts again.
The sound sequence plays on, and a delay run out leaves the weapon ready.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.UpdateStatus
member.summary: Lets go the triggers the tick let go of, at the end of the holder's tick: Weapon_UpdateStatus (igi2 0x51E370).
member.remarks: A primary trigger let go part way into a burst — more than one round a pull, some but not all fired, and fewer than the clip holds — is kept down to finish the burst. Any other is let go: the release goes out with how long the trigger was down and the holder's frame, taken with its inaccuracy, and the trigger and its count start again.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.Reload
member.summary: Reloads the weapon in hand, Weapon_Reload (igi2 0x51E120) as Weapon_SingleReloadHandler (0x51D440) does it.
member.remarks: The delay is cleared. Each fire type that uses ammunition starts its count of rounds fired again and, unless it is loaded by hand, takes what its clip lacks — a single round when it is reloaded a round at a time — from what is carried, no more than there is, or all of it with ammunition that never runs out. An empty weapon is then ready.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.ReleaseAutoFire

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.ReleaseTriggers
member.summary: Lets go of both triggers and clears the status, as death and water do.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.ReleasePrimaryIfBusy
member.summary: Lets the primary trigger go if the weapon is busy, as a soldier waiting out its fire delay does (HumanAIContent_ShootAtTarget, humanaicontent.c): a weapon not ready has its primary let go and is made ready; a ready one is left alone, so a wait between bursts lets go once, not every tick.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.TakeKickback

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.SingleFire(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2FireMessage@)
member.summary: The shot itself, Weapon_SingleFireHandler (igi2 0x51CD40).
member.remarks: A fire type that must be loaded by hand fires from what is carried and needs as many rounds carried as it takes; any other needs them loaded. A delay not run out holds the shot. The position comes back from centimetres and the orientation from its angles, and the fire type's handler fires; whatever it fired or delayed is spent and noted, the weapon has fired, and the kick is kept for the holder.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponFiring.SingleRelease(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ReleaseMessage@)
member.summary: A trigger let go, Weapon_SingleReleaseHandler (igi2 0x51D1D0).
member.remarks: Letting go the primary stops the weapon firing on by itself. A fire type with a release handler runs it, and the weapon is ready after. A release that fires spends it as a shot does, except that a weapon loaded by hand loses twice the rounds it fired, floored at none (the original's arithmetic).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2WeaponTables
member.summary: The session's ammunition and weapons, read from WEAPONS/ammo.qvm and WEAPONS/weapon.qvm at start-up.

remarks.para: Flow_CreateHandler (igi2 0x401600) loads the ammunition first, then the weapons, before the materials, the AI's settings and the player's tuning, each into a container that lasts the session.

Each AmmoType takes the next number of a count that is never reset (AmmoType_CreateHandler, 0x43AE20), and unless its Ammo ID is AMMO_ID_UNDEFINED that name becomes a script constant with the number (AmmoType_UpdateInternalDataHandler, 0x43AF10); the weapon script names its ammunition by those constants. Each WeaponType does the same with its own count and its Weapon ID (WeaponType_CreateHandler, 0x434FA0; WeaponType_UpdateInternalDataHandler, 0x435270), which the player's tuning and the levels' scripts then name. The first weapon is the undefined one, so the real ones count from one.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.Weapons.Igi2ZoomFire
member.summary: What a Zoom does when fired and when the zoom keys step it: Zoom_WeaponFireHandler (igi2 0x525B20) and Zoom_WeaponZoomHandler (0x525CC0).

remarks.para: Fired, a zoom held by a human toggles the human's view. Down, the view's zoom comes off, back to the default fields of view, and so do the weapon's overlay and its status. Up, a zoom whose overlay type is a task type puts the view into zoom mode and the overlay up; one whose is not only marks the weapon zoomed. Either way the view steers to the zoom's widest scale, a third of the gap a tick. It fires nothing, with no delay.
The zoom keys step a zoomed weapon's aim by its step factor, narrower or wider, as far as its scales reach, and sound its zoom sound at the view.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2TerrainDiscard
member.summary: The ground one takes away, as the box the renderer tests against.
member.param: The west edge, in world units.

remarks.para: Two dimensions, not three. DiscardTask_IsDiscardVertex (igi2ed 0x65A670) compares X against the pair at +344/+348 and Y against +356/+352 and stops there; the task's Z and its height are never in the test. A discard is a column through the whole world, which is what lets one box under a hangar floor remove the hillside the hangar is cut into whatever height either happens to sit at.

Axis-aligned, even for a rotated task. DiscardTask_UpdateInternalDataHandler (0x65AEE0) forms the four floats straight from Width and Height without consulting the task's gamma. The rotated corners it computes just above feed the editor's 2D discard mesh and the task's collision cube instead, so a turned DiscardTask removes ground its own outline does not cover. That is the original's behaviour rather than an approximation of it.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.DiscardTask
member.summary: A hole cut through the ground — I.G.I. 2's DiscardTask, the box inside which the terrain is neither drawn nor stood on.

remarks.para: This is the sequel's answer to the same problem I.G.I. 1 solves with DiscardTerrain. A level that cuts a vehicle ramp into a hillside, or sinks a hangar below it, has geometry where the height field still says there is ground; without the hole the terrain draws straight through the ramp's floor and the player walks on a hillside inside a building. The first game removes octree cubes; this one removes render vertices, which is a much smaller mechanism because the sequel's ground is a height field rather than a mesh.

A triangle goes only when all three of its corners do. TerrainRender_DrawFace (igi2ed 0x66AAB0) ANDs the three per-vertex flags that TerrainRender_CalculateRenderVertex (0x66A740) wrote, so the ground is cut back to the box rather than around it, and the last ring of triangles inside the edge stays to close the hole against whatever building sits in it.

The ground query obeys the same flag: Terrain_GetNextZHandler (0x62E620) tests the point before it accepts a surface, so a body over a discard gets no terrain at all and falls to the collision mesh of whatever was built there.

Four of the twenty-four shipped levels declare the type — location1/level1 for its vehicle hangar, location1/LEVEL6, location2/LEVEL2 for its two sewer mouths, and the multiplayer map sandstorm for ten of them. Levels that declare it also declare the three parameters below and no others; the editor's own Update push button is not in level data.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.FlatSkyTask
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's sky: a graded dome with scrolling layers over it.

remarks.para: Declared by all 24 shipped levels. The dome is five colours — a top, two middles and two bottoms — interpolated down its height by SkyDome_InterpolateVertexColour (igi2ed 0x5719B0) into a vertex buffer built once (SkyDome_InitialiseVertexBuffer, 0x5717E0). The clouds are separate: each child is one scrolling texture drawn over the dome.
is not only the sky's. The host clears the frame to it so the horizon meets backing of the same colour rather than black, which is the same arrangement Project I.G.I. uses.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.FlatSkyLayerTask
member.summary: One scrolling cloud layer over the sky dome.

remarks.para: The texture name is rebased, not used as written. FlatSkyLayer_FixFilename (igi2ed 0x653890) strips whatever directory the level authored and re-prefixes the bare file name with MISSION:textures/ — keeping the extension, which is why a sky layer resolves to a loose .tga beside the level rather than to anything in an archive.

So a level may author any path it likes and the engine will look in exactly one place. That is worth reproducing rather than trusting the authored string: the two agree on the shipped data and would diverge the moment a mod authored a path.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.ForestTask
member.summary: One stand of trees — I.G.I. 2's Forest: one model, an area, and a placement file listing every instance of it.

remarks.para: A forest is a single model drawn many times. names it, the placement comes from MISSION:forest_<id>.dat, and says how many of that file's records to use. The engine builds a BSP tree over them at load time — Forest_CreateBSPTree (igi2.exe 0x59F350) — which is what line-of-sight and tracing queries run against, so a forest is collidable geometry and not decoration.

Nine of the eighteen parameters are editor tools. The three PushButtons do not hold a value at all: they are the buttons that randomise the area, rebuild the placement and rebake the light. Brush size and Brush draw/delete are the painting tool, and the four Random … range values are what that tool draws with — they shape the file when it is written and are not consulted again once it exists.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2BirdFlockTask
member.summary: A flock of birds, I.G.I. 2's BirdFlock (birdflock.c): up to a hundred birds wheeling about a point, each drawn as two flapping wings, while the camera is within its cutoff distance.

remarks.para: BirdFlock_UpdateInternalDataHandler: at most a hundred; each bird's swings start at nought, each period forty to 1240 ticks.

BirdFlock_RunHandler, while seen: each swing counts on, and past its period starts again with a period of twenty to sixty seconds times a fiftieth of its radius. A bird stands at the sum of the sines of its first two swings times the radius across, of its last two up the other way, and of its first and last times ten metres up, each swing a turn a period, half a turn on; it flies the way it moved.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2DrawableScene
member.summary: Turns what an I.G.I. 2 level places into the shared a renderer draws.

remarks.para: There is one world renderer, and both games use it. WorldRenderer takes a of s — a position, an orientation, an , the pack behind it, a and a lightmap name — and every one of those is a thing both games have. It named no task type, no model id and no asset path, so it moved from Game.Igi1 into the shared presentation layer unchanged.

What is not shared is how a level becomes placements. walks Project I.G.I.'s task tree and knows its type names, its parameter names and even its security-camera model ids. This is the sequel's equivalent, and it is short because the four milestones before it already answered the hard parts: the scene walk found the placements, the pack table resolved the virtual models, and the lightmap index bound the bakes.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2EditBoneObjTask
member.summary: An animated figure, I.G.I. 2's EditBoneObj (editboneobj.c): the actors of cutscenes and the people standing about, a boned model that plays a list of clips in turn, blending from one to the next, with a weapon in hand and blinking eyes.

remarks.para: EditBoneObj_UpdateInternalDataHandler: the model is given its face (); with a rig, a clip controller is made (two and a blend when its transition time is above nought), at its time factor, smoothed when asked; the list starts at its first clip. After load its weapon expression, when it has one, names the weapon model.

EditBoneObj_RunHandler: its children run; when the clip ends, the next in the list (split on commas, spaces, tabs and new lines) plays, blending over its transition time, back to the first when the list loops; a list that does not loop holds its last. While it blinks, a pause of up to 150 ticks is drawn from the module's blink stream, then three frames close the eyes by 1, 0.6 and 0.2.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2FixedFunctionSun
member.summary: The light I.G.I. 2 shines on an object that has no baked lightmap: the level's Dirlight as a Direct3D directional light, over the GlobalLight's object ambient.

remarks.para: An unlightmapped object is lit by the fixed-function pipeline, and by nothing else. Direct3DRender_SetGenericStateRigid (igi2ed 0x56CA90) sets a material of pure white diffuse and ambient, D3DRS_LIGHTING = 1 and D3DRS_COLORVERTEX = 0; Direct3DRender_SetTextureStateRigid (0x56CE10) makes stage 0 MODULATE(TEXTURE, DIFFUSE). The model's vertex format carries no colour (XYZ|NORMAL|TEX), so DIFFUSE there is what Direct3D computes per vertex: saturate(D3DRS_AMBIENT + Σ light.Diffuse · max(N · L, 0)). The lightmapped state block (0x56CFD0) turns lighting off; a bake replaces all of this.

The one light. DirlightQTask_DrawCallback (0x657680) hands each Dirlight to Lightsource_NewDirlight (0x41C860), whose renderer half Direct3DRender_AddLightsource (0x56C750) builds a D3DLIGHT_DIRECTIONAL with Diffuse = the keyframe's front colour, no specular, no ambient, and Direction = the negated sun vector — so the vector the keyframe stores points towards the sun, and a face whose normal agrees with it is the lit one. The back colour is stored on the light and never reaches Direct3D. The Affects objects flag is stored beside it and, at run time, not consulted either: the light is added unconditionally.

The ambient. GlobalLightQTask_DrawCallback (0x6534E0) passes the object category's ambient to Lightsource_SetAmbientlight (0x41C990), which the same renderer half writes as D3DRS_AMBIENT. See for which category.

The direction, from the binary rather than from plausibility. DirlightKeyframeQTask_UpdateInternalDataHandler (0x6573C0) builds Real32x9_Create(0, 2π − Beta, 2π − Gamma) and rotates (1, 0, 0) by it. Real32x9_Create (0x605F40) composes Gamma · Beta · Alpha from Real32x9_CreateGamma (0x6061F0, a rotation about Z) and Real32x9_CreateBeta (0x6061B0, about Y), applied to a column vector, which works out to . The elevation is Beta itself and Gamma is the azimuth. This differs from the shared , which was fitted to Project I.G.I.'s data and yields (−sin β, 0, cos β); that reading is left alone here because it is Project I.G.I.'s, and the sequel computes its own.

member.param: The flat light every unlightmapped vertex receives, linear.
The sun's diffuse colour, from the keyframe's Front Color, linear.
The unit vector towards the sun, in the world's Z-up frame.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2Forest
member.summary: A level's forests: the trees each Forest task scatters, placed in the world.

remarks.para: A forest is not placed the way anything else is. The task says where the stand is, how big it is and which model to use; the trees themselves live in a separate forest_<taskId>.dat beside the level, keyed by the same level task id its baked lightmaps use.

A tree's stored position is local to its task. Forest_DrawTrees (igi2ed 0x64AC80) culls the stand against a square of AreaSize * 4096 centred on the task, and walks its BSP over ±AreaSize * 2048 — local coordinates, half the area either side. The shipped files agree: X and Y run to a few hundred metres either side of nothing.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestBsp
member.summary: A stand's trees indexed the way Forest_CreateBSPTree indexes them, and walked the way Forest_DrawTrees1_Optimized walks them.

remarks.para: Despite the name the engine gives it, this is a two-dimensional k-d tree, not a BSP: the split plane is always axis-aligned and the axis alternates with depth. Forest_BuildBSPTree (igi2ed 0x64C610) sorts the sub-range it is given with Forest_TreeObjectCompareX (0x649180) at even depths and Forest_TreeObjectCompareY (0x6491C0) at odd ones — it picks the callback with depth & 1 — takes the element at count >> 1 as the node, and recurses on the two halves either side of it. Every tree is a node; there is no leaf bucket.

Before the tree is built, Forest_RemoveOutsiders (0x64C6D0) drops every tree whose local X or Y is beyond AreaSize * 2048 and lowers the stand's tree count to match, so the root region is exactly the square the stand is culled against.

Forest_GenerateHeightDataRecursively (0x64C940) then fills each node's height range bottom-up: the minimum is the lowest of the node's own foot and its children's minima, the maximum the highest of its children's maxima and its own crown, which is position.z + scale.z * modelHeight. The walk needs it because the k-d tree partitions X and Y only — Z has to come from somewhere, and it comes from here.

Tie-breaking may differ from the original. The engine sorts with QVector_QSortPart, an unstable quicksort, so two trees sharing a coordinate can land either way round and pick a different median. The tree that results is a different tree with the same contents; it culls the same trees but its node order is not guaranteed to match the engine's.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestBsp.Cull(OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestClipPlanes@,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Action{System.Int32})
member.summary: Walks the tree near to far, handing every tree the clip planes keep to a visitor.
member.param: The stand's clip planes, with their origins relative to the camera.
The stand's centre relative to the camera, in world units.
How far a tree may lean out of its node's region; see .
The tree model's radius in model units, before the per-tree scale.
The tree model's Z extent in model units, before the per-tree scale.
Called with the index into the stand's tree list of every visible tree.
member.returns: How many trees were handed to .

remarks.para: This is Forest_DrawTrees1_Optimized (igi2ed 0x64AE60). It carries a running region — four floats the original calls avCoords, ordered max X, min X, max Y, min Y and seeded with the stand's square — and tightens one side of it on the way down, which is what gives each node a box to be tested against without storing one.

The order is near to far. The child on the camera's own side of the split is descended first, then the node's own tree is drawn, then the far child — so a stand comes out roughly front to back, which is what the sorted foliage pass wants and what fills the depth buffer early for the rest.

A node's box is inflated by and a tree's is not. The region only bounds tree positions; a tree standing on the edge of it still has a crown hanging outside, and the margin is what stops the walk cutting that crown off. The per-tree test is exact, so it needs no such slack.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestBsp.MarginOf(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: How far a tree may lean out of the region its position sits in, in world units.
member.param: The tree model's radius in model units.
member.returns: The margin every node's box is inflated by.
member.remarks: (max(rangeX, rangeY) * 0.5 + 1) * modelRadius, computed once at the top of Forest_DrawTrees1_Optimized from ptForest + 1548, + 1552 and the model radius at + 1560. The two ranges are the scatter the editor's brush scales with, so 1 + range / 2 is the largest a tree in the stand can have been scaled to and the product is the widest crown the stand can hold. It is a bound on the data rather than a fudge factor.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestClipPlanes
member.summary: The plane set a forest is culled against: the four frustum sides, the near plane, and the two that cut the stand off at its view distance.

remarks.para: Forest_SetUpClippingPlanes (igi2ed 0x64B550) builds these in view space and then rotates them into world space by the inverted view matrix, offsetting each origin by the view point — which is why a plane here is a point and a normal rather than a normal and a distance. The origins are kept relative to the camera so the whole test stays in single precision.

A box is out of sight when every one of its eight corners is strictly on a single plane's positive side. Straddling planes never reject, which is what makes this test conservative and cheap: one plane, eight dot products, an early out on the first plane that rejects.

The two cut-off planes are not a far plane. They sit at cutoff / halfTangentX along the view axis with normals turned ±halfFovX / 2 off it, so the pair meets the frustum's own side planes at the same range and approximates a cylinder rather than a slab — a stand fades at the same distance ahead as it does in the corner of the eye. Forest's View cutoff (m) (limited by object lod settings) is what sets the range; Forest_UpdateInternalDataHandler converts it with * 4096 into ptForest + 1536, and it is that field the plane origin is built from.

remarks.para: Forest_IsAABBOutOfSight (igi2ed 0x64B200), and the mask is the reason it is worth porting rather than replacing with a sphere test. A box wholly inside a plane has every descendant wholly inside it too, so the plane never has to be tested again down that branch — which is what makes a deep tree cheap near the middle of the screen, where most of the trees are.

Not ported: the original also caches, in the node itself, the index of the plane that last rejected it, and tests that one first the next time round. That survives across frames, so it needs a mutable node; the mask here is a walk parameter and needs nothing.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ForestLod
member.summary: Picks a tree's level of detail from how far away it is.

remarks.para: ForestRender_GetLOD (igi2ed 0x57D680), the branch a model with a distance table takes. The distances are stored in the model's LOD virtual model as five floats — the four level thresholds and then the cut-off — and each is scaled by the largest of the tree's three per-axis scales before it is compared, so a tree scattered half again as large stays detailed half again as far out.

The last band is the one that matters here. Past every threshold the tree is compared against the cut-off, and beyond it the function returns −1 and ForestRender_Draw (0x57CA90) returns without drawing anything at all. That is the per-tree half of the view distance the two extra clip planes cut whole subtrees at.

What could not be read. The distance table lives in the MTP LOD virtual model, which this port does not parse, so nothing here can supply the retail thresholds; a caller with one level passes the stand's own view cut-off and gets exactly the retail behaviour for a one-level model. And ForestRender_vLODBiasInversed, the factor the last band's distance is scaled by, is read at 0x57D8B8 and written nowhere in igi2ed.exe — so in the editor it is zero and the cut-off never fires. Its companion ForestRender_vLODBiasSquared is (bias * 16 + 1)², and since the distance has already been multiplied by that under the square root, the reciprocal 1 / (bias * 16 + 1) is the only value that makes the comparison a comparison of real distances. That is an inference from the arithmetic, not something read.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2GameMaterials
member.summary: The session's materials, read from material/material.qvm (GameMaterial_LoadParameters, igi2 0x433940) after the weapons.

remarks.para: The script sets a row with SetActiveMaterial(n) (GameMaterial_SetActiveMaterialCB, 0x432D40) and fills it with DefineQMaterial, the half that draws, and DefineGameMaterial, the half the game reads. The row is what a collision face's material and a terrain material's iGameMaterial name.

DefineGameMaterial reads its arguments in a fixed order: the name, five numbers, eight walking and eight running steps, the landing, three falls of a body, the rain, six bullet strikes, two grenade strikes and a knife strike. Then come two effects, each a task type and as many further arguments as that type's parameter reader takes: a GunShotEffect takes six; a type with no reader takes none.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2Ground
member.summary: The ground an I.G.I. 2 level puts under a body: the height field its tiles describe, sampled the way the original samples it.

remarks.para: The whole query is Terrain_VertexFunction (igi2 0x5706F0). It picks the tile, interpolates the four samples around the point over one of the cell's two triangles, and returns the height relative to the level's terrain together with that triangle's normal. Terrain_GetNextZHandler (0x572E80) — the handler every ground query in the game reaches through — then adds the Terrain task's own Z and keeps the surface only when it falls between the two ends of the probe.

The normal is the triangle's, not a smoothed one. The original derives it from the same two differences the height came from, so the surface a body slides on is exactly the surface it stands on. (TerrainMap_GetNormal takes a central difference over neighbouring samples instead, but that one belongs to the lightmap bake and nothing else calls it.)

A removes the ground here too. Terrain_GetNextZHandler tests the point against DiscardTask_IsDiscardVertex (igi2 0x5D1850) before it accepts a surface, so a body over one of the level's discard boxes gets no terrain at all and falls to whatever collision mesh was built in the hole. The renderer applies the same boxes, which is what keeps the surface a body stands on the surface it can see.

Placed objects are not in here. The body's own query already casts at the world's collision meshes and keeps whichever surface is higher, exactly as it does for the first game, so a crate or a building floor still wins over the ground beneath it.

member.remarks: A height field makes the swept test exact rather than approximate: the body is above the surface at one end and below it at the other, so the crossing is where the gap changes sign. member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2LensflareTask
member.summary: A lens flare, I.G.I. 2's Lensflare (lensflaretask.c): sprites strung along the line from where the sun stands on the screen through the screen's centre, fading in and out as the sun is seen or hidden.

remarks.para: LensflareQTask_GetDirlightDirectionAndColor: its direction and colour are its Dirlight's, the one its id names, or its parent without one, as the light stands.

LensflareQTask_EnterHandler, each frame, unless lens flares are off: the sun is put far along its direction from the camera and projected; nearer than ten thousand, or off the display, it is not seen, otherwise as much of it is seen as a line of sight from the camera towards it lets through (Lensflaretask_CalcIntensity). The intensity eases to that, four fifths kept a frame; from a hundredth up its items are drawn, each at its position along the line to the sun's mirror through the display's centre, in whole pixels.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2LightmapIndex
member.summary: A level's baked object lightmaps, indexed by the task each one belongs to.

remarks.para: I.G.I. 2 does not name a lightmap after the object it lights. It names it after the object's level task id — the first argument of Task_New — which is why binding lightmaps needs the scene to carry that id and why exists.

The name is written by LightmapInfo_AddLightmapVirModelToEnumeration (igi2ed 0x625A20) as %04d_%04d_%1d.olm, or %04d%c_%04d_%1d.olm when the object has more than one group of models: a task id, an optional group letter, a model index and a level of detail counted from one.

This reads the index out of the archive rather than recomputing it. The model index is a running counter the original increments as it walks a task and its children (RigidDynCubeObj_EnumerateLightmapVirModelsHandler, igi2ed 0x6266E0), and reproducing it would mean reimplementing one enumeration handler per task type — for a number the shipped archive already states. The task id is the part a renderer cannot get from the archive, and that is the part this binds.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2LightmapIndex.Read(OpenIGI.Formats.Ilff.IresArchive)

member.summary: Builds the bare file name the original identifies a lightmap by.
member.param: The model group, or zero for an object with only one.
The model's position in the object's enumeration.
The level of detail, counted from one.
member.returns: The file name, with no directory and no alias.
member.exception: A part is outside what the format can express.

remarks.para: The inverse of , and written to match the original's two format strings exactly: the lettered form is taken only when the group is non-zero, which is why index zero of — the ! — is never emitted.

Bare, not alias-qualified, and that is not a simplification. The original sprintfs exactly this and looks it up in LightmapInfo_ptLightmapVirModelHashTable; it never builds a resource path. Nor could it usefully: 23 of the 24 shipped levels register their entries as LOCAL:lightmaps/…, but location3/level1 registers LOCAL:missions/location3/level1/lightmaps/…. A renderer that constructed a resource name would work on every level but that one. So loading goes through , which is whatever the archive actually says, and this method is for identity and diagnostics.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2DirlightTask
member.summary: The sun or moon, I.G.I. 2's Dirlight (dirlighttask.c): a directional light whose direction and front and back colours are keyed through the day by its DirlightKeyframe children, drawn as a sprite of its texture where it stands in the sky.

remarks.para: DirlightQTask_UpdateInternalDataHandler spans its keyframes' times; each frame the viewport's time of day sets it (DirlightQTask_DrawCallback, DirlightQTask_SetTime), and a time it is not already at updates it.

DirlightQTask_Update: without keyframes it is dark, pointing straight up. With every keyframe at one time it is the first's. Otherwise a keyframe at the time is it; else the latest before and the earliest after the time bracket it, and it is the one before when there is none after, or the two are at one time, or the one after when there is none before. Between two it is interpolated: its colours straight, its direction turned from the earlier's about the axis across the two by the angle between them, scaled by how far between them the time is.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2MissionCatalogue
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's missions, as its own mission.qvm scripts publish them.

remarks.para: The walk is the shared one — a script per mission directory — and the reader is not. I.G.I. 2's DefineMission takes fourteen arguments where the first game's takes eleven, and the difference is not a suffix: the fourth argument of the first game is the id of the mission that follows, and I.G.I. 2 has nothing of the kind.
Read from Mission_DefineMissionCB (igi2 0x40E2D0), which is unambiguous because it evaluates each argument into a fixed offset of a 1,968-byte record:
remarks.code: 0 int the mission id, checked for uniqueness against every mission already registered 1..4 four SINGLE-CHARACTER strings, packed big-endian into one word the code calls aazGameModeID: 'S','N','G','L' for the campaign and 'M','U','L','T' for a multiplayer map 5 string the name key (+16, 32 bytes) 6 string the description key (+48, 1024 bytes) 7 string a tag, empty everywhere (+1072, 32 bytes) 8 string the mission directory (+1104, 256 bytes) 9 string the common directory (+1360, 256 bytes) 10 string the level directory (+1616, 256 bytes) 11 string the common pack name (+1872, 32 bytes) 12 string the level pack name (+1904, 32 bytes) 13 string the briefing sprite (+1936, 32 bytes)
remarks.para: Those offsets are what settles the packs. Game_CreateHandler (igi2ed 0x4469A0) reads the descriptor at +0x550, +0x750, +0x650 and +0x770 — which are 1360, 1872, 1616 and 1904, the common directory and its pack name and then the level directory and its pack name. So the four packs a mission opens are the two global ones and the two this record names, and neither the order nor the names are inferred from the directory tree.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2MissionCatalogue.Campaign
member.summary: Gets the missions of the single-player campaign, in the order the scan found them.
member.remarks: By mode rather than by a chain, because there is no chain: the first game names the mission that follows each one and I.G.I. 2 does not. Ordering a campaign is therefore a separate question, and this only says which missions are in one.

remarks.para: The campaign's missions by ascending id, then everything else the same way. Ascending id is the campaign's own grouping rather than an arbitrary sort: a mission's id is its location and its level read together — location1/level1 is 11 and location2/LEVEL2 is 22 — so ascending id walks the locations in turn and the levels within each.

The mode filter is what makes it work. The shipped multiplayer maps take ids 1, 5 and 100, which are below and above the campaign's 11 to 36; sorting every mission by id together would put two deathmatch maps ahead of the first mission of the game.
It is still a listing order and not a progression. Nothing in this title's DefineMission says which mission follows which, so a real campaign flow has to come from the front end.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2MissionCatalogue.InProgressionOrder

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2ModelTable
member.summary: What a level's .mtp packs turn a placed model name into: a mesh file, and the textures it wears.

remarks.para: A level does not name mesh files. It names virtual models, and a pack's VNAM and INST chunks turn each one into a mesh from MODS plus a set of material slots. Several virtual models routinely share a mesh: location1's rsg1_1, rsg2_1 and rsg3_1 all draw model rsg_1 with texture sets [2,3], [2,4] and [2,5] — one soldier mesh, three uniforms. That is why a name like rsg3_1 is nowhere on disk while the level asks for it 900 times.

Two packs are consulted, nearest first: the level's own, then its location's common one. That is not a convention invented here — MTP_ParseMTP (igi2.exe 0x4F5DE0) resolves a model index below against the pack being parsed and one at or above it against the head of the pack list, which is the common pack. already carries that rule.

The container is the same one Project I.G.I. uses, chunk for chunk, so reads both games unchanged. What differs is only how much of it a level leans on: the first game names most of its meshes directly, and the sequel routes its characters through the table.

member.summary: Builds a table over the packs a level has open, in the order the original loads them.
member.param: The packs, nearest the front of the original's list first: the global common pack, then the new pack, then the location's, then the level's.
member.exception: No packs were given, or one of them is .

remarks.para: The first pack to name a model wins, which is the opposite of what this used to do. MTP_VirModel_GetPtr (igi2.exe 0x4F4CA0) walks MTP_tMTPList from the head and returns the first match; MTP_Load appends, so the head is the pack loaded first. A level therefore cannot override a name the global pack already has.

The order comes from Game_CreateHandler, which loads four packs in a fixed sequence behind its own loading-screen captions: common ("Loading common resource archive..."), new, the location ("Loading LOCATION..."), then the level ("Loading LEVEL MTP...").

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2PlacementBinding
member.summary: Which parameters one task type names its model, its position and its facing with.

remarks.para: Most placeable types agree, and a dozen do not. The great majority of I.G.I. 2's world objects declare Model, Position and Orientation under exactly those names, which is what lets walk them all without a class for any of them. But a type whose model moves has a name for where it starts rather than where it is — a Door carries Position start, a Lift carries Start Position — and a type that owns two models qualifies both — a Switch has an On model and an Off model, an SCamera a Holder Model and a Camera Model.

The original needs no such table: every one of these types has its own create handler, and each one binds its own parameter block to a ModelObj and registers it in the world's cube tree, so the draw walk sees them all alike whatever their parameters are called. This is the port's equivalent — the parameter names those handlers read, as data, so that one walk still collects every type.

member.param: The parameter naming the model to draw at rest.
The parameter naming the position, a Vector3d in engine units.
The parameter naming the Euler orientation, a Vector3f of alpha, beta and gamma. Empty when the type carries a single angle instead; see .
The parameter naming a lone gamma angle, for a type that turns about the world's up axis and nothing else. Read only when finds nothing.
The parameter naming the model to draw instead when is set. Empty for a type with one model.
The boolean parameter that selects . Empty for a type with one model.
The parameter naming a SECOND model this one carries, placed on the first's magic vertex. Empty for a type with one model. See for the handlers.
The parameter naming the mounted model's own tilt, in radians. Empty when it simply inherits the host's facing.
The parameter naming the mounted model's own turn about the up axis, ADDED to the host's. Empty when it simply inherits the host's facing.

The magic task type of the attach point the mounted model hangs on, instead of the host itself: it is placed on that attach object's first magic vertex, facing as it faces, and walked after it. Empty to mount on the host.
Every model parameter the type's lightmap enumerator walks, in the order it walks them. Empty for a type with one model, which is then index zero. See .

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2PortalCulling
member.summary: I.G.I. 2's portal culling: which sectors a camera can see from the one it stands in, and through what part of the screen.

remarks.para: The runtime half of , ported from three functions of the shipped binaries: Sector_IsPortalVisible (igi2.exe 0x587D10, igi2ed.exe 0x428850), SectorObject_TraverseSector (0x588830) and SectorObject_RequestSector (0x588470), with the entry point SectorObject_EnterHandler (0x588A70) supplying the starting rectangle. The dedicated server and the editor carry the same code; the editor's copy differs only by a call to Sector_DrawPortal that draws the outline it just computed.

This is rectangle narrowing, not frustum clipping. A portal is projected, its triangles are clipped to the screen, their bounding box is taken, and that box is intersected with the rectangle the portal was itself seen through. Nothing carries a plane set forward; the whole state passed between sectors is four floats.

What is deliberately not modelled. The original picks a level of detail per candidate (ModelObj_GetLOD) and skips one that returns -1; it also skips a portal whose per-object status byte is zero, which is what a door drives (Sector_SetPortalOpen, igi2ed.exe 0x42AFD0, writes ptSector + iPortal + 352). LOD is ignored, and the open/closed state arrives through the isPortalOpen delegate, which answers from the doors.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi2.World.Igi2PortalCulling.DefaultTraversalBudget
member.summary: How many sector traversals one Visit will run before it stops.
member.remarks: A port-only guard; the original has none. SectorObject_RequestSector recurses unconditionally even when the sector already has a request, so the only thing bounding the original is the discard list, which forbids a sector from re-entering itself on the path it is already on. That makes the traversal explore every simple path through a container's sectors, which is factorial in the worst case and merely fine on the shipped levels. This cap keeps a pathological level from hanging a frame.

member.remarks: SectorObject_EnterHandler empties any requested sector's ptClipWindowsList holding more than four and pushes the request's union in their place, before it draws.

remarks.para: SectorObject_EnterHandler (igi2.exe 0x588A70): the building the camera stands in is started from the camera's room through the whole display area, and so is any building while the camera stands in none. A building seen while the camera stands in another one is started from its shell once per clip window the outside was reached through, all into one request pool. A sector left holding more than windows is given their union instead.

The candidate set is the starting sector's building, for the whole walk. SectorObject_TraverseSector begins its candidate loop at SectorObject_ptActiveSectorObject -- the building being drawn, whose shell is a sector in its own right -- and then walks that building's ptSectorContainer, its rooms, however deep the recursion has gone. member.remarks: The matrix is stored row by row, and it takes the object's own frame to the world's: world = M · local. A collision line handler multiplies with these exact floats, so a pose that is a bit off is a wall that is a bit off.

member.param: The angles alpha, beta and gamma, in radians.

remarks.para: The rotation is Z(gamma) · Y(beta) · X(alpha), built as gamma's matrix multiplied by beta's and the result by alpha's, every term in general form. The zero terms drop out exactly, which leaves each element one product or one two-product sum, each truncated to 24 bits.

member.summary: The pose of an object hanging off this one: ModelObj_CreateAttachObject (igi2 0x56D0B0).
member.param: The attachment record from this object's model.

remarks.para: The record's matrix is used transposed, its first two columns as the first two rows, and the third row is rebuilt as their cross product. That is then turned by this object's matrix, and the record's position is turned and added to this object's position. Each row of each product sums its three terms in its own order.
The position sum is a register sum too, so an attached object's world position is truncated to 24 bits.

member.returns: Alpha, beta and gamma, each in radians from zero to a whole turn.

remarks.para: With the X axis more than a ten thousandth off vertical, alpha is fpatan of m7 over m8, beta of −m6 over that length, and gamma as gives it; with it vertical, alpha is fpatan of −m5 over m4 and gamma is zero.
